subevent.name: After the meeting, shared takeaways with colleagues and formulated the second-quarter plan.
subevent.description: After the review meeting, Yu Xiaowei exchanged insights with colleague Su Lishan in the pantry of the AIA Wan Chai office about retaining existing clients in the first quarter, and shared her own tips in customer service. Then she returned to her workstation and wrote in her meeting notebook the plan for the second quarter to focus on high-net-worth clients, including the target list and initial contact strategies.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Wan Chai District - AIA Building

name: Spring health consultation and dietary adjustment
description: On February 15, Yu Xiaowei called ahead to make an appointment with Dr. Zhou Wenbin, a family doctor at Hong Kong Sanatorium & Hospital, and went to the hospital at noon on February 19 to consult about nutritional supplements for spring training and knee protection. Dr. Zhou advised increasing calcium intake and paying attention to cooling down after runs. She took careful notes and adjusted her diet structure on the same day.

subevent.name: Booked a spring consultation with the family doctor.
subevent.description: Yu Xiaowei called the office of Dr. Zhou Wenbin, the family doctor at Hong Kong Sanatorium & Hospital, in advance to book a noon spring health consultation for February 19, and confirmed that the consultation would focus on training nutrition supplements and knee protection.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Hong Kong Sanatorium & Hospital

subevent.name: Go to Hong Kong Sanatorium & Hospital for consultation.
subevent.description: During the lunch break on February 19, Yu Xiaowei set out from her office in the AIA Building on Gloucester Road, Wan Chai District, and took the MTR to Hong Kong Sanatorium & Hospital in the Central and Western District. After arriving, she went to Dr. Zhou Wenbin's consultation room and began her spring health consultation.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Hong Kong Sanatorium & Hospital

subevent.name: Consult on spring training nutrition and knee protection
subevent.description: In the consultation room at Hong Kong Sanatorium & Hospital, Yu Xiaowei consulted her family doctor, Zhou Wenbin, in detail about a nutritional supplement plan and knee protection measures for spring marathon training. Dr. Zhou advised her to increase her calcium intake (such as milk and soy products) and to make sure she cooled down fully after running. Yu Xiaowei carefully wrote down the advice and discussed her diet and training habits with the doctor.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Hong Kong Sanatorium & Hospital - Consulting Room

subevent.name: Adjust training and diet structure
subevent.description: Following Dr. Zhou's advice, Yu Xiaowei adjusted her daily diet plan immediately after returning home that day, adding calcium-rich foods (such as fresh milk, cheese, and broccoli) and optimizing her post-run recovery meal, while also incorporating the post-run cool-down steps into her training log to ensure they would be carried out properly later.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Kowloon City District - home

name: Family car replacement decision and execution.
description: On the evening of July 24, Yu Xiaowei and her husband Zhang Weiming discussed changing cars at home, settled on the Toyota Prius as the candidate model, and made a car-viewing plan. Her mother Chen Meiling gave advice. On the afternoon of the 25th, Yu Xiaowei went alone to a car dealership in Wan Chai to view cars and ask for prices, and obtained a formal quotation. On the morning of Saturday the 26th, the couple test-drove the Prius together, were very satisfied with its quietness and fuel economy, and exchanged views on environmental protection and practicality. On the afternoon of the 27th, they formally signed the car purchase contract and paid the down payment, then picked up the whole family and drove to the top of Victoria Peak for a drive to celebrate the successful car change. The new car improved the family's travel experience and also symbolized her husband's identification with the transition to environmentally friendly technology, subtly echoing his earlier expressed longing for craftsmanship.

subevent.name: Family discussion about replacing the car
subevent.description: On the evening of July 24, Yu Xiaowei and her husband Zhang Weiming had an in-depth discussion in the living room about replacing the family's old petrol car. Referring to online information, they identified the energy-efficient and environmentally friendly Toyota Prius hybrid as the candidate model, and preliminarily agreed on a budget and a car-viewing plan. Her mother, Chen Meiling, was nearby offering advice and support.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Kowloon City District - living room at home.

subevent.name: Went alone to a car dealership in Wan Chai to look at cars and ask about prices
subevent.description: On the afternoon of July 25, Yu Xiaowei took the MTR alone to the Toyota showroom on Gloucester Road in Wan Chai to inspect the exterior and interior of the Toyota Prius. She asked the sales consultant in detail about the configuration, fuel consumption, warranty, and price, and returned home after obtaining a formal quotation that included purchase discounts.
subevent.location: Toyota showroom, Wan Chai District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

subevent.name: The husband and wife test-drove a Toyota Prius together.
subevent.description: On the morning of Saturday, July 26, Yu Xiaowei and her husband Zhang Weiming went together again to the car dealership in Wan Chai. Accompanied by a sales consultant, they test-drove the Toyota Prius hybrid. They took turns driving, experiencing the vehicle's quietness, smooth acceleration, and low fuel consumption. During the test drive, they had a pleasant discussion about the shift to eco-friendly technology and practical family needs, and were very satisfied with the vehicle's performance.
subevent.location: Toyota showroom and surrounding roads, Wan Chai District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

subevent.name: Signed the car purchase agreement and paid the down payment, and the whole family went for a drive at Victoria Peak.
subevent.description: On the afternoon of July 27, Yu Xiaowei and Zhang Weiming went to a car dealership in Wan Chai to formally sign the Toyota Prius purchase contract, pay the down payment, and complete the vehicle pickup procedures. Afterward, the couple drove home to pick up her mother Chen Meiling, their son Zhang Zixuan, and their daughter Zhang Yuxin. The whole family then drove to Victoria Peak for a sightseeing drive, enjoying the peak views along the way and experiencing the comfort and convenience of the new car to celebrate the successful car change.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Wan Chai District - Toyota showroom and Victoria Peak

name: My husband got up early to prepare a training-day breakfast and had breakfast with me, chatting
description: Yu Xiaowei's husband, Zhang Weiming, woke up early on the morning of September 16, 2025, and used his knowledge of nutrition to prepare a high-protein, low-GI breakfast for his wife on her training day. The couple then had breakfast together at the table, chatting about the husband's career transition plans and their daughter's progress in ballet class. Yu Xiaowei felt her husband's support and the warmth of her family.

subevent.name: Husband got up early to prepare breakfast for training day
subevent.description: Yu Xiaowei's husband Zhang Weiming got up early on the morning of September 16, 2025, and went alone into the kitchen of their home at 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong. Using knowledge learned from a nutrition class, he carefully cooked a high-protein, low-GI training-day breakfast, including pan-fried chicken breast, boiled eggs, whole-wheat toast, and a cup of unsweetened soy milk. He carefully controlled the heat and portions to ensure balanced nutrition, providing energy support for his wife's long-distance run training that day.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon City District - home kitchen

subevent.name: Husband and wife had breakfast together and chatted casually.
subevent.description: After getting up, Yu Xiaowei had breakfast with her husband Zhang Weiming at the dining table. The two rarely had time alone together, and while eating they talked about her husband's intention to change careers (from an air conditioner repair technician to studying nutrition and considering obtaining a nutritionist qualification), as well as their youngest daughter Zhang Yuxin's recent progress and funny moments in ballet class. Yu Xiaowei felt her husband's quiet support and the warmth of her family, and her heart was full of gratitude.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon City District - Home dining room

name: Afternoon tea with close friend Lin Jiaxin, asking about each other's recent lives.
description: On May 23 (Friday), Yu Xiaowei invited her close friend Lin Jiaxin via WeChat to meet at a cafe in Sham Shui Po on Saturday afternoon. On May 24 (Saturday) afternoon, Yu Xiaowei went to the cafe in Sham Shui Po to meet Lin Jiaxin. They ordered a pot of Earl Grey tea and two desserts, and chatted about recent work and family life. Yu Xiaowei specifically asked about the career concerns Lin Jiaxin had previously expressed, and Lin Jiaxin admitted that she had started considering switching teaching grade levels. The two encouraged each other and agreed to take the children on a short trip together during the summer vacation.

subevent.name: Inviting Lin Jiaxin to Saturday afternoon tea
subevent.description: On Friday, Yu Xiaowei contacted her close friend Lin Jiaxin via WeChat on her phone, inviting her to meet at a coffee shop in Sham Shui Po on Saturday afternoon. Lin Jiaxin gladly agreed and confirmed they would meet at 3 p.m.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon City District - home

subevent.name: Going to a coffee shop in Sham Shui Po
subevent.description: On the afternoon of Saturday, May 24, Yu Xiaowei set out from her home on Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City, took the MTR to Sham Shui Po District, and walked to the café she had agreed on with Lin Jiaxin.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Sham Shui Po District MTR station and streets

subevent.name: Afternoon tea with Lin Jiaxin and catching up on how she has been
subevent.description: Yu Xiaowei met her close friend Lin Jiaxin at a café in Sham Shui Po. The two ordered a pot of Earl Grey tea and two desserts, and chatted about their work and family lives. Yu Xiaowei specifically asked about the career worries Lin Jiaxin had previously mentioned. Lin Jiaxin admitted that she had begun to consider switching to a different grade to teach. The two encouraged each other and agreed to take the kids on a short trip together during the summer holiday to strengthen the children's friendship.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - coffee shop in Sham Shui Po District

name: Had dinner with running buddy Shen Peiwen in Shenzhen, where we encouraged each other and kept our friendship strong.
description: On Sunday, May 25, Yu Xiaowei had a meal with her running buddy Shen Peiwen at MixC World in Shenzhen. The two talked about their recent frustration with work and stalled training. Shen Peiwen encouraged her to maintain her fitness, and they agreed to resume systematic training in the fall, aiming to break her half-marathon personal record in the second half of the year. Yu Xiaowei also asked about Shen Peiwen's family situation. They cheered each other on, and their friendship deepened in the relaxed atmosphere.

subevent.name: Depart for MixC World in Shenzhen
subevent.description: At 9 a.m., Yu Xiaowei set out from her home on Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong, took the MTR East Rail line to Luohu Port, crossed the border, then transferred to Shenzhen Metro Line 1 to Hi-Tech Park Station and walked to MixC World; the whole trip took about 1.5 hours. Meanwhile, her running partner Shen Peiwen set out from her home in Kwun Tong District, Hong Kong, and took the same route to Shenzhen. The two agreed to meet at the main entrance of MixC World at 11 a.m.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Kowloon City District / Shenzhen - Nanshan District, MixC World

subevent.name: Meet up at MixC World and start the group dinner.
subevent.description: Yu Xiaowei and Shen Peiwen met on time at the main entrance of MixC World mall in Nanshan District, Shenzhen. After an excited hug and greetings, they went to a Hong Kong-style café inside the mall and sat down. They ordered familiar favorites such as pineapple buns with butter, Hong Kong-style milk tea, and wonton noodles, chatting while they ate in a relaxed and pleasant atmosphere.
subevent.location: Shenzhen - Nanshan District, MixC World Hong Kong-style Tea Restaurant

subevent.name: Get-together to share updates and encourage each other
subevent.description: During the meal, Yu Xiaowei confided to Shen Peiwen about her frustration over how heavy work pressure had halted her training recently. Shen Peiwen also shared the troubles brought by family trivia. Shen Peiwen encouraged Yu Xiaowei not to give up on her fitness, and proposed that the two resume systematic training starting in autumn, with the goal of challenging personal bests in the half marathon in the second half of the year. Yu Xiaowei, in turn, asked about Shen Peiwen's family situation and offered emotional support. The two agreed to check in with each other for morning runs every week and supervise each other via WeChat.
subevent.location: Shenzhen - Nanshan District, MixC World Hong Kong-style Tea Restaurant

subevent.name: The dinner ended, and everyone headed back to Hong Kong.
subevent.description: At 1:30 pm, the two finished their meal and walked around MixC World mall to aid digestion, taking photos as souvenirs. Then they said goodbye at the metro station. Yu Xiaowei returned the same way through Lo Wu Port to Hong Kong and got home in Kowloon City District at 3:00 pm. Shen Peiwen returned through Futian Port to her home in Kwun Tong District. After arriving, she sent Yu Xiaowei a message saying she had arrived safely.
subevent.location: Shenzhen - Nanshan District MixC World / Hong Kong - Kowloon City District

name: Organized a list of prospective clients and sent personalized proposal emails.
description: On October 10, Yu Xiaowei used the customer management system at the office to filter out about 20 potential clients in the Shenzhen area and, during her lunch break, sent each of them an email containing a personalized insurance plan and suggestions for scheduling a consultation, in order to make up for client attrition.

subevent.name: Organize list of potential clients in Shenzhen.
subevent.description: After learning that the major Shenzhen client had been taken by Zhou Minyi, Yu Xiaowei immediately used the company's customer management system in her office to screen and compile a list of about 20 potential clients in the Shenzhen area who had not yet closed deals, in preparation for follow-up contact.
subevent.location: Office at AIA Building, Wan Chai District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

subevent.name: Send a personalized insurance proposal email
subevent.description: During her lunch break, Yu Xiaowei wrote and sent personalized insurance plan emails one by one based on each potential client's basic information and needs. The emails included a brief self-introduction, product highlights, and suggestions for booking a consultation. She sent 20 emails in total.
subevent.location: Office at AIA Building, Wan Chai District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Took my daughter to ballet class on February 15 and 22.
description: Daughter Zhang Yuxin's ballet class resumed after the Spring Festival. On the mornings of Saturday, February 15 and 22, Yu Xiaowei got up early, helped her daughter change into her leotard and dance shoes, and was driven by her husband Zhang Weiming to the dance school together. Seeing her daughter look serious at the barre, she felt gratified and also enjoyed this regular parent-child time.

subevent.name: Take daughter to ballet class (February 15)
subevent.description: On Saturday morning, Yu Xiaowei got up early, helped her daughter Zhang Yuxin change into a ballet leotard and ballet shoes, and her husband Zhang Weiming drove them together to the dance school in Kowloon City District. Yu Xiaowei watched from outside the classroom as her daughter practiced seriously at the barre, feeling gratified. The class ended after about 1.5 hours, and the family of three returned home.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - a ballet school in Kowloon City District

subevent.name: Drop daughter off at ballet class (February 22)
subevent.description: On Saturday morning, Yu Xiaowei and her husband Zhang Weiming again took their daughter Zhang Yuxin to the dance school for her ballet class. The same routine: getting up early to prepare, driving to school, watching the class, picking her up, and enjoying their regular parent-child time.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - a ballet school in Kowloon City District

name: Morning run with running buddy Shen Peiwen, followed by breakfast and a heart-to-heart talk
description: Around 6:30 a.m. on September 23, 2025, Yu Xiaowei set out from her home at 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City, Hong Kong, and went to Victoria Park to meet her running partner Shen Peiwen. The two then completed a 10 km morning run together along the designated track in the park at similar paces, chatting about running rhythm and recent life. After the run, at about 8 a.m., they shared breakfast at a Hong Kong-style tea restaurant near Victoria Park. Shen Peiwen noticed that Yu Xiaowei seemed preoccupied and took the initiative to ask. Yu Xiaowei opened up about work pressure, team management challenges, and lingering doubts with her close friend. Shen Peiwen listened patiently, shared stress-relief methods she used with students in her teaching, and encouraged her, saying, "Some things can't be rushed." The two agreed to continue running together the next week, and Yu Xiaowei felt a sense of ease she hadn't felt in a long time.

subevent.name: Going to Victoria Park
subevent.description: At about 6:30 a.m. on the morning of September 23, 2025, Yu Xiaowei changed into her running gear and set off from her home at 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong, walking or taking a short ride to the main entrance of Victoria Park to meet Shen Peiwen.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Victoria Park Entrance

subevent.name: Completed a 10 km morning run
subevent.description: At around 7 in the morning, Yu Xiaowei and Shen Peiwen completed a 10 km morning run together along the designated track in Victoria Park. Their paces were similar, and they chatted about running rhythm and recent life along the way, in a relaxed atmosphere.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Victoria Park running track

subevent.name: Morning run followed by breakfast and heart-to-heart talk at a cha chaan teng
subevent.description: After the morning run, around 8 o'clock, Yu Xiaowei and Shen Peiwen went together to a Hong Kong-style tea restaurant near Victoria Park, ordered pineapple buns with butter, wonton noodles, and Hong Kong-style milk tea, and chatted over breakfast. Shen Peiwen noticed that Yu Xiaowei seemed troubled, so she asked. Yu Xiaowei poured out her work pressure, team management challenges, and doubts about her close friend. Shen Peiwen listened patiently, shared the stress-relief methods she used when interacting with students in elementary school teaching, and encouraged her: "Some things can't be rushed." The two felt relaxed during the pleasant conversation, and Yu Xiaowei's mood clearly improved.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - tea restaurant near Victoria Park

name: Ms. Wu Xiuying extended a studio invitation and subsequent discussions
description: On Saturday, September 6, 2025, Yu Xiaowei went to the Cantonese embroidery studio for a class. During the break, the teacher Wu Xiuying felt dizzy. Yu Xiaowei and He Meiling took care of her attentively and tidied up the studio. Moved by this, the teacher proposed that they run the studio together. That evening, Yu Xiaowei discussed it with her husband Zhang Weiming at home. Two days later, she communicated online with He Meiling, and they had a preliminary discussion about future division of labor and arrangements.

subevent.name: Setting off for the Cantonese embroidery studio
subevent.description: On Saturday morning, Yu Xiaowei prepared her embroidery tools and materials, set out from her home on Prince Edward Road West in Kowloon City District, took the MTR to Wu Xiuying's Cantonese Embroidery Studio at 245 Lai Chi Kok Road in Sham Shui Po District, and prepared to attend the afternoon Cantonese embroidery class.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - MTR and Sham Shui Po District - Wu Xiuying’s Cantonese Embroidery Studio

subevent.name: Attended the Cantonese embroidery class.
subevent.description: Yu Xiaowei and He Meiling, who had just been transferred back to Hong Kong, attended a class together at the Cantonese embroidery studio of teacher Wu Xiuying to learn traditional Cantonese embroidery stitches. The class atmosphere was harmonious; the three chatted about their recent lives while embroidering.
subevent.location: Hong Kong, Sham Shui Po District - Wu Xiuying's Cantonese Embroidery Studio

subevent.name: Teacher Wu felt dizzy during the break
subevent.description: During the break, Teacher Wu Xiuying suddenly felt dizzy, swayed, and almost fell. Yu Xiaowei and He Meiling immediately went over to help her to a sofa, brought her warm water, and asked with concern. They confirmed that the teacher was only feeling unwell due to low blood sugar, and she gradually recovered after resting.
subevent.location: Hong Kong, Sham Shui Po District - Wu Xiuying's Cantonese Embroidery Studio

subevent.name: Proactively tidy up the studio
subevent.description: While Teacher Wu was resting, Yu Xiaowei and He Meiling took the initiative to tidy up the somewhat messy studio, organizing the silk threads, cleaning the workbench, arranging the embroidery frames and fabrics, and sweeping the floor, leaving the studio looking brand new.
subevent.location: Hong Kong, Sham Shui Po District - Wu Xiuying's Cantonese Embroidery Studio

subevent.name: Teacher Wu extended an invitation to jointly run the studio.
subevent.description: Teacher Wu Xiuying was deeply moved by Yu Xiaowei's and He Meiling's attentiveness and sense of responsibility, and formally proposed that if they were willing, they could jointly run this Cantonese embroidery studio in the future. The teacher said that she was advanced in age and hoped to entrust this craft and the studio to trustworthy disciples. Yu Xiaowei felt honored by this trust and also realized the responsibility on her shoulders.
subevent.location: Hong Kong, Sham Shui Po District - Wu Xiuying's Cantonese Embroidery Studio

subevent.name: Go home after class
subevent.description: After the class ended, Yu Xiaowei and He Meiling said goodbye to Teacher Wu and left the studio. Yu Xiaowei took the MTR back to her home in Kowloon City District. Along the way, she felt mixed emotions—excited by the teacher’s recognition, yet thinking about how to respond to this important invitation.
subevent.location: On the commute from Sham Shui Po to Kowloon City District, Hong Kong

subevent.name: Discussing the studio invitation with her husband.
subevent.description: After returning home in the evening, Yu Xiaowei told her husband, Zhang Weiming, in the bedroom in detail about what had happened at the studio that day and Teacher Wu's invitation. The two analyzed the potential time, energy, and financial impact of running the studio together. Zhang Weiming expressed support but reminded her to plan carefully.
subevent.location: Hong Kong, Kowloon City District - bedroom at Yu Xiaowei's home

subevent.name: Online communication with He Meiling about follow-up arrangements
subevent.description: The next morning on Sunday, Yu Xiaowei had a video call with He Meiling via WeChat to further exchange views on Teacher Wu's invitation. Both agreed that this was a valuable opportunity to pass on Cantonese embroidery, and they preliminarily explored the general direction of future division of work, course arrangements, and studio restructuring, agreeing to find a time to discuss the details with Teacher Wu together.
subevent.location: Kowloon City District, Hong Kong - living room of Yu Xiaowei's home.

name: Marathon training: pace rebounding but with a sense of detachment
description: From September 1 to 10, 2025, Yu Xiaowei continued her marathon training plan, completing a 16-kilometer long run and several interval runs in succession, with her pace clearly recovering compared to the previous month. However, after each training session she felt a sense of detachment; the joy of running was gradually replaced by a mechanical rhythm, and she even began to doubt the real meaning of being so committed to training.

subevent.name: Interval running training (September 1)
subevent.description: Following her marathon training plan, Yu Xiaowei went alone to Kowloon Tsai Sports Ground for 400m x 10 sets of interval running training. Each set was a sprint at 85% of maximum heart rate, with slow jogging recovery between sets. After the session, she felt a sense of accomplishment from the improved pace, but it was followed by a strong sense of detachment, as the joy of running was replaced by mechanical rhythm.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon Tsai Sports Ground

subevent.name: Interval running training (September 4)
subevent.description: Yu Xiaowei did 800m x 6 sets of interval training at Fa Hui Park in Mong Kok, with an average pace 3 seconds faster than last week. She focused on stride cadence and breathing during the workout, but after finishing, the sense of alienation from mechanical repetition reappeared, and she began to question the meaning of continuing high-intensity training.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Mong Kok Flower Market Park

subevent.name: 16-kilometer long-distance training run
subevent.description: In the early morning, Yu Xiaowei did a 16-kilometer long-distance training run along the Tseung Kwan O waterfront promenade, running at a steady marathon pace. During her post-run stretching, she felt physically great, but her mind felt detached—the usual scenery and sea breeze seemed blurry, and only a distinct sense of emptiness cooled her passion for running.
subevent.location: Hong Kong SAR - Tseung Kwan O Waterfront Promenade

subevent.name: Training diary and inner reflection.
subevent.description: The ten-day training cycle came to an end. Yu Xiaowei wrote a training diary in her home study, recording pace data and psychological changes in detail. Having compared it with her previous love of running, she now only felt a sense of detachment after mechanically executing the plan. She decided to talk to her coach Zhao Zhiming next week about adjusting the training rhythm to rediscover her original passion for running.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon City District - Home Study

name: Missed Japanese class and switched to fragmented self-study; the study plan was disrupted.
description: After her mother-in-law sprained her ankle on April 14, Yu Xiaowei and her husband took turns caring for her, and evening time was nearly squeezed dry. The first Japanese class originally scheduled for Monday had to be skipped; subsequent attempts to make up the class could not guarantee continuous attendance, so she could only use scattered moments to learn vocabulary on a mobile app. From April 16 onward, she switched to fragmented self-study mode, and the original systematic course had to be suspended.

subevent.name: Mother-in-law accidentally sprained herself.
subevent.description: Yu Xiaowei's mother-in-law, Li Shufen, sprained her lower back at home in Kwun Tong District and called Yu Xiaowei. After work, Yu Xiaowei hurried to her mother-in-law's home (Golden Bridge Mansion, 45 Hong Ning Road, Kwun Tong District), checked the injury, and consulted family doctor Zhou Wenbin for advice. After confirming that an emergency room visit was not needed, she applied a medicated plaster to her mother-in-law's back and helped her rest, while also discussing the follow-up care plan with her husband, Zhang Weiming.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kwun Tong District - mother-in-law's home

subevent.name: The couple took turns caring for her mother-in-law.
subevent.description: Because her mother-in-law had sprained herself and had difficulty moving, Yu Xiaowei and her husband Zhang Weiming urgently discussed and made a temporary care plan: on the evening of April 14, Yu Xiaowei would stay overnight at her mother-in-law's home to accompany her; during the day on April 15, Zhang Weiming would take leave to care for her and take the children to and from school; in the evening, Yu Xiaowei would take over after work. The two adjusted their original family division of labor to ensure that her mother-in-law was cared for without affecting the children's school attendance, but the time Yu Xiaowei originally used for evening Japanese study was completely occupied.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kwun Tong District - mother-in-law's home and Kowloon City District - own home

subevent.name: Yu Xiaowei stayed overnight to accompany her mother-in-law.
subevent.description: In the evening, Yu Xiaowei arrived at her mother-in-law Li Shufen's home in Kwun Tong District with daily necessities, helping her wash up, prepare dinner, and make the bed. She stayed by her side throughout the night, checking on her every two hours and assisting with her nighttime bathroom needs to ensure her safety and comfort. During the night, Yu Xiaowei spoke with her husband Zhang Weiming by phone to confirm the next day's arrangements and make sure the children were settled.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kwun Tong District - mother-in-law's home

subevent.name: Zhang Weiming looked after his mother during the day and handled the children's pick-up and drop-off.
subevent.description: Zhang Weiming took a day off. In the morning, he first took his son Zhang Zixuan to school and his daughter Zhang Yuxin to kindergarten, then went to his mother-in-law's home in Kwun Tong District to take care of Li Shufen, assisting her with rehabilitation activities, preparing lunch, and helping her take her medication. In the afternoon, Zhang Weiming picked up the children on time and brought them home to do their homework. Meanwhile, he reported his mother-in-law's condition to Yu Xiaowei by phone and waited for her to take over after work.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kwun Tong District - mother-in-law's home

subevent.name: Yu Xiaowei took over evening care after work.
subevent.description: After finishing work at AIA Insurance, Yu Xiaowei took the MTR from Wan Chai back to her home in Kowloon City District for a short rest, then hurried to her mother-in-law's home in Kwun Tong District. She did a handover with Zhang Weiming, learned about her mother-in-law's condition during the day, then prepared dinner for her, helped with nighttime care, and chatted with her to ease her mind. Yu Xiaowei stayed overnight at her mother-in-law's home again to ensure she was safe through the night.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kwun Tong District - mother-in-law's home

subevent.name: Absent from the first Japanese language class
subevent.description: Yu Xiaowei was forced to miss the first class of the structured Japanese course originally scheduled for Monday evening, April 16, because she needed to continue taking care of her mother-in-law. She asked for leave in advance via WeChat from the teacher at the training institution and requested the course replay materials, but that night she was too exhausted from caregiving to watch the recording in time. This absence disrupted her continuous study plan.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kwun Tong District - mother-in-law's home

subevent.name: Switched to fragmented self-study mode
subevent.description: After two days of struggle, Yu Xiaowei discussed it with her husband in the family WeChat group and formally decided to suspend the structured Japanese course and switch to a fragmented self-study mode. On the subway during her commute home, she used her phone to download a Japanese learning app (such as Duolingo), set daily goals, and planned to use scattered moments during lunch breaks, commutes, and after the children fell asleep to learn vocabulary and basic grammar. She told her teacher that she wanted to defer resuming the course and felt regret over the course fees she had already invested.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - MTR carriage and Kowloon City District - home

subevent.name: Learning Japanese in spare moments
subevent.description: Starting April 19, Yu Xiaowei used fragmented moments squeezed between caring for her mother-in-law and household chores — 30 minutes on the commuting subway, 20 minutes during lunch break, and 15 minutes after the children were asleep — to repeatedly practice Japanese words and short phrases through a mobile app. Because the time was fragmented and often interrupted, progress was slow, and each week she could complete only 30% of the originally planned course content. She felt frustrated but was unwilling to give up, and occasionally played audio late at night while doing Cantonese embroidery to keep her ears trained. By May 31, her mother-in-law had largely recovered, and her Japanese was still only at the stage of simple greetings and memorized nouns.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - MTR, AIA Insurance office, her living room and bedroom

name: First attempt at sports massage to relieve lactic acid buildup
description: On the evening of September 20, after two consecutive days of high-intensity interval running, Yu Xiaowei's right calf gastrocnemius muscle became noticeably stiff. She booked a 30-minute deep tissue massage at a sports rehabilitation center in Wan Chai. After assessing her running posture, the massage therapist focused on releasing her quadriceps and fascia bands. When it was over, her legs felt light as feathers, and she marveled, "So massage requires more courage than running itself." This experience made her realize the importance of active recovery, and she added a weekly fascia gun relaxation session to her plan.

subevent.name: Noticed muscle stiffness and booked a massage.
subevent.description: During the day on September 20, 2025, after two consecutive days of high-intensity interval running, Yu Xiaowei felt tightness in the gastrocnemius muscle of her right leg. She booked an appointment by phone or through an online platform at a sports rehabilitation center in Wan Chai, reserving a 30-minute deep tissue massage service for that evening.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - home in Kowloon City District (when booking)

subevent.name: Go to the rehabilitation center for deep tissue massage
subevent.description: On the evening of September 20, 2025, Yu Xiaowei left home and headed to the sports rehabilitation center in Wan Chai District, Hong Kong. Upon arrival, the massage therapist first assessed her running posture, then focused on deep release of the quadriceps and fascial bands of her right leg. The entire process lasted 30 minutes. After the massage, Yu Xiaowei felt her legs as light as feathers and praised the sensation of the massage.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Wan Chai District - A Sports Rehabilitation Center

subevent.name: Summarize the experience and formulate an active recovery plan.
subevent.description: On the evening of September 20, 2025, Yu Xiaowei returned home and, reflecting on the sports massage experience, realized the importance of active recovery. She decided to incorporate a weekly massage gun relaxation session into her regular recovery plan to prevent lactic acid buildup and muscle stiffness.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Kowloon City District - home

name: Meet long-time client Mrs. Chen for the policy anniversary review and sign the upgrade plan
description: On April 7, 2025, Yu Xiaowei organized the insurance policy documents for the family of client Chen Meiling (Mrs. Chen) in her home study and drafted an upgrade plan, while also reserving a seat at Tsui Wah Restaurant in Causeway Bay for the next day. On the afternoon of April 8, Yu Xiaowei met with Mrs. Chen at Tsui Wah Restaurant, reviewed her family's medical, savings, and children's education policies one by one, and recommended the upgraded hospital medical rider and the pre-underwriting campaign for high-end medical insurance. Mrs. Chen approved the plan and signed a letter of intent for insurance on the spot, agreeing to go through the formal application procedures next week.

subevent.name: Prepare insurance policy review materials
subevent.description: Yu Xiaowei organized the medical, savings, and children's education policy documents for client Chen Meiling (Mrs. Chen)'s family in her home study, analyzed the current coverage, and drafted an upgrade plan (hospital medical rider) based on inflation and the family's new needs. At the same time, she called Tsui Wah Restaurant in Causeway Bay, Hong Kong, to reserve a table for the afternoon of April 8, 2025, fully preparing for the next day's meeting.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - home study

subevent.name: Met with Mrs. Chen for policy review and recommendations
subevent.description: On the afternoon of April 8, 2025, Yu Xiaowei went to Tsui Wah Restaurant in Causeway Bay, Hong Kong, to meet with client Chen Meiling (Mrs. Chen). In a booth of the cha chaan teng, Yu Xiaowei analyzed one by one the AIA insurance policies currently held by Mrs. Chen's family (medical insurance, savings insurance, children's education insurance). Based on the latest medical inflation and the family's new needs, she recommended an upgraded inpatient medical rider and introduced the upcoming pre-underwriting activity for the high-end medical insurance. Mrs. Chen showed strong interest and asked in detail about the rider's coverage and premium.
subevent.location: Causeway Bay, Hong Kong - Tsui Wah Restaurant

subevent.name: Sign the letter of intent and arrange the follow-up procedures.
subevent.description: At the end of the meeting, Mrs. Chen Meiling highly approved of the upgraded plan recommended by Yu Xiaowei and signed the letter of intent for the upgraded inpatient medical rider on the spot. Yu Xiaowei agreed with Mrs. Chen to visit her home next week (specific time to be confirmed) to complete the formal insurance application procedures, and promised to have the full set of application documents ready by then. Yu Xiaowei also reminded Mrs. Chen about the pre-underwriting campaign for high-end medical insurance. Mrs. Chen said she would consider it and thanked Yu Xiaowei for her attentive service.
subevent.location: Causeway Bay, Hong Kong - Tsui Wah Restaurant

name: During the Qingming Festival, the whole family visited the graves and listened to stories of the struggles of their forebears.
description: On the evening of April 3, 2025, Yu Xiaowei and her husband Zhang Weiming prepared tomb-sweeping supplies. On the morning of April 4, Qingming Festival, the whole family drove to Xili Cemetery in Shenzhen to pay respects together with her uncle and grandmother. The eldest uncle, Yu Guoliang, recounted how the great-grandfather built up the family from scratch. Grandmother Liang Shufang added the story of the grandmother using Cantonese embroidery to supplement the family income. For the first time, Yu Xiaowei heard the complete family story and was deeply moved. On the way back, she shared her reflections with her family. After returning home, she organized her notes and looked through old photos, feeling nourished by the family spirit.

subevent.name: Preparing tomb-sweeping supplies
subevent.description: On the night before Qingming, Yu Xiaowei and her husband Zhang Weiming went to the supermarket and incense shop near Prince Edward Road West in Kowloon City District to buy flowers, incense, candles, offerings, and other supplies for tomb sweeping, and confirmed the next day's route and vehicle condition.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon City District - Prince Edward Road West

subevent.name: The whole family set off for the cemetery in Shenzhen
subevent.description: On the morning of the Qingming Festival, April 4, 2025, Yu Xiaowei set out from home with her husband Zhang Weiming, son Zhang Zixuan, daughter Zhang Yuxin, mother Chen Meiling, and father Yu Guoqiang. They drove the family car through the border crossing to a cemetery in Shenzhen, Guangdong Province. On the way, her father Yu Guoqiang briefly explained the tomb-sweeping procedure for the day.
subevent.location: Hong Kong SAR – Kowloon City District to a cemetery in Shenzhen, Guangdong Province

subevent.name: Visit the grave to pay respects and listen to family stories.
subevent.description: The whole family arrived at Shenzhen Xili Cemetery (fictional) and held a tomb-sweeping ceremony at the ancestral graves, laying out offerings, burning incense, and bowing. Uncle Yu Guoliang recounted how the great-grandfather had moved south from Guangzhou to Shenzhen and built a life from scratch. Grandma Liang Shufang added details about how the great-grandmother had supplemented the family income with her Cantonese embroidery skills during the years of material scarcity. Yu Xiaowei heard these family stories in full for the first time and was deeply moved.
subevent.location: Xili Cemetery, Shenzhen, Guangdong Province

subevent.name: Return trip after the tomb sweeping
subevent.description: After the tomb-sweeping, Yu Xiaowei's family had lunch with her uncle and grandmother at a restaurant near the cemetery, then said goodbye. The whole family drove back to their home in Kowloon City, Hong Kong. On the way, Yu Xiaowei talked with her mother and husband about the family stories heard that day and reflected on the family's resilient spirit.
subevent.location: Shenzhen, Guangdong Province to Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

subevent.name: After returning home, organized and reflected
subevent.description: Back home in the evening, Yu Xiaowei organized the family stories she heard during the day into written records in the study, and browsed through old photos provided by her mother Chen Meiling. Thinking of the connection between her beloved Cantonese embroidery skills and her grandmother, she felt nourished by her family's strength, and the pressure from work and family eased.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon City District - Home Study

name: Start a healthy eating plan and use an app to record three meals a day.
description: Starting June 1, in order to support her autumn half-marathon training and overall health management, Yu Xiaowei downloaded and began using a nutrition management app on her phone, recording her food intake at every meal. She gradually cut down on fried food when eating out and increased her intake of vegetables, fruit, and high-quality protein, and drank a glass of honey lemon water after yoga. After a month of this, she felt more energetic during the day and noticeably less sleepy in the afternoon.

subevent.name: Continue to keep food records and make adjustments.
subevent.description: Starting June 3, Yu Xiaowei used a nutrition app to record three meals a day and made healthy bento boxes to reduce eating out. On June 6, based on the first week's records, she adjusted the staple food at dinner and drank honey lemon water after yoga class. On June 15, she went to the street market to buy ingredients and raised her protein intake target. On June 21, according to the app feedback, she replaced the dinner staple with sweet potatoes. On June 29, she did a stage summary and planned to add more leafy greens next month. During the period, she kept recording consistently, with occasional missed entries backfilled the next day, and overall adherence was high.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon City District - kitchen and dining room at home on Prince Edward Road West, and the cha chaan teng near the office

subevent.name: Started a healthy eating log and made the first day's bento box
subevent.description: Yu Xiaowei completed her personal health profile setup on the nutrition management app, recording in detail the food types, approximate portions, and cooking methods for breakfast (one cup of Hong Kong-style milk tea, one pineapple bun with butter), lunch (homemade bento: blanched choy sum, pan-fried chicken breast, white rice), and dinner (at home: steamed fish, garlic broccoli, millet porridge). She decided to eat out less starting today, switch to bringing her own homemade lunch on workdays, and deliberately walk past street food stalls after work to avoid buying fried fish balls and other fried snacks.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon City District - kitchen and dining room at home on Prince Edward Road West

subevent.name: Implement the first week of dietary adjustments and record yoga-day supplements
subevent.description: Yu Xiaowei checked this week's food diary on the app and found that the proportion of staple foods at dinner was too high, so she decided to replace part of the white rice with brown rice. That day, after her yoga class, she went home and made a drink with honey and lemon. Full-day diet record: breakfast (one bowl of wonton noodles), lunch (homemade bento: cucumber salad, braised beef, brown rice), dinner (at home: stir-fried choy sum, tomato and tofu soup, one sweet potato). She also added the lunch entry she had missed the previous day.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon City District - home kitchen on Prince Edward Road West

subevent.name: Weekend shopping for healthy ingredients and optimizing protein intake
subevent.description: On a weekend morning, Yu Xiaowei went to Kowloon City Market to buy fresh vegetables (broccoli, choy sum, spinach), fruit (apples, blueberries), chicken breast, tofu, brown rice and other ingredients. After returning home, she portioned and refrigerated the ingredients, and prepared semi-finished meal components for the next workweek's bento lunches. She recorded the day's shopping list in the app and adjusted her diet plan: raising the daily protein target from 60g to 70g and increasing the frequency of soy product intake.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon City District - Kowloon City Market and home kitchen

subevent.name: Adjust dinner nutrition ratio based on app feedback
subevent.description: Yu Xiaowei checked the nutrition ratio analysis for the past two weeks on the app and found that the carbohydrate proportion at dinner was relatively high (over 50%), so she decided to replace the dinner staple with sweet potatoes or pumpkin. That day she logged her meals: breakfast (one cup of Hong Kong-style milk tea, one egg sandwich), lunch (a homemade bento: stir-fried broccoli, pan-fried tofu, one sweet potato), dinner (at home: boiled shrimp, stir-fried spinach, half a sweet potato). She also planned to do weekly meal prep every Sunday going forward.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon City District - Prince Edward Road West - home dining room

subevent.name: Summarize dietary records for the phase and plan next month's approach.
subevent.description: Yu Xiaowei completed the last day of diet logging on the nutrition management app (Breakfast: Hong Kong-style milk tea, pineapple bun; Lunch: homemade bento: stir-fried chicken breast with broccoli, brown rice; Dinner: at home: steamed sea bass, garlic lettuce, millet porridge). She exported this month's diet report and found that overall calorie control was good, protein intake met the standard, but vegetable variety was somewhat limited. Based on this, she planned to increase leafy vegetable intake next month and planned to add a new healthy menu in July.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon City District - Home study on Prince Edward Road West

subevent.name: Month-end review and summary of the healthy eating plan
subevent.description: On the evening of June 30, Yu Xiaowei used a nutrition management app at home to review her diet records for the past 30 days. She found that her average daily calorie intake was controlled at around 1,800 kcal, the protein ratio increased from 15% to 22%, and her intake of vegetables and fruits increased significantly. Combined with how she felt physically, she noticed that she had more energy during the day, and afternoon drowsiness was markedly reduced, while her weight dropped by about 1 kg. She saved a screenshot of the monthly summary in the app and shared it with her husband and mother in the family WeChat group, receiving encouragement from family members. She then planned to continue using the app in July and add a once-a-week intermittent fasting attempt for weight management. The entire review process lasted about 40 minutes, during which she drank honey lemon water and took notes on her personal reflections.
subevent.location: Hong Kong SAR - Kowloon City District - living room at home on Prince Road West

name: Started the Cantonese embroidery piece Daughter's World: Autumn. He Meiling sent special embroidery threads and proposed a Shenzhen exchange delegation.
description: On Saturday, October 12, Yu Xiaowei officially began work on the Cantonese embroidery piece Daughter's World: Autumn. He Meiling had sent over a batch of special embroidery threads from Shenzhen and mentioned on the phone that many white-collar workers in Shenzhen were taking an interest in traditional crafts, and perhaps they could organize an exchange group to come to Hong Kong for a hands-on experience. As Yu Xiaowei spread out the embroidery cloth, she thought this might be a new opportunity to preserve and promote Cantonese embroidery.

subevent.name: Receive the special embroidery thread parcel sent by He Meiling
subevent.description: At her home at 328 Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong, Yu Xiaowei received a courier package sent from Shenzhen. After opening it, she found that He Meiling had specially given her a batch of special embroidery threads (including pearlescent silk and gradient silk threads). She carefully examined the colors and textures of the threads and sorted them into the craft material cabinet, preparing for her upcoming Cantonese embroidery work.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon City District - home at 328 Prince Edward Road West

subevent.name: Yu Xiaowei and He Meiling discussed the Shenzhen exchange group proposal over the phone
subevent.description: After receiving the embroidery thread, Yu Xiaowei proactively made a WeChat voice call with He Meiling, who was far away in Shenzhen, to thank her for the special embroidery thread. During the call, He Meiling mentioned that many white-collar workers in Shenzhen had developed a strong interest in Cantonese embroidery and suggested organizing a small exchange group to come to Hong Kong to experience the craft. Yu Xiaowei carefully noted the discussion points, including the possible number of visitors, schedule, and activity format, and said she would consider the idea and plan to discuss follow-up implementation with Teacher Wu Xiuying.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon City District - home at 328 Prince Edward Road West

subevent.name: Start creating the Cantonese embroidery piece "Daughter's World: Autumn"
subevent.description: After finishing the phone call with He Meiling, Yu Xiaowei spread the embroidered fabric on the embroidery frame in her living room and officially began creating her new Cantonese embroidery work, "Daughter's World: Autumn." She first used a water-soluble pen to outline the planned autumn-themed design on the white satin (fallen leaves, chrysanthemums, and the back view of a little girl), then selected appropriate colors from the embroidery threads and started the first stitches. She spent the whole afternoon on the drafting and basic stitching, feeling happy and full of anticipation.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon City District - home at 328 Prince Edward Road West

name: Taking the orange tabby Fei Zai for his annual check-up and health management.
description: On March 1, Yu Xiaowei called Love Pet Clinic in advance to make an appointment for the annual check-up. On the morning of March 2, she took her orange tabby cat Fatty to the clinic for the check-up and vaccination. The veterinarian noted that Fatty was 6% overweight and recommended controlling his diet and increasing exercise. On the way home she bought a cat teaser wand, and as soon as she got home she adjusted his food portions and switched to low-calorie cat food. That afternoon she began playing with Fatty for 15 minutes every day. She recorded the check-up results and the health management plan in the family memo so she could keep tracking them.

subevent.name: Booked a pet clinic checkup.
subevent.description: The day before, Yu Xiaowei called Caring Pet Clinic in Kowloon City District to book a morning appointment on March 2 for her pet orange cat, Fatty, for the annual checkup and vaccination.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Kowloon City District - Love Pet Clinic

subevent.name: Take Feizai for the annual physical exam and vaccinations.
subevent.description: On the morning of March 2, Yu Xiaowei took her orange tabby cat Feizai in a pet carrier to Aixin Pet Clinic for a full physical examination, weight measurement, and annual vaccination. The veterinarian said Feizai was 6% overweight and recommended limiting treats and adding interactive games to help him lose weight.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Kowloon City District - Love Pet Clinic

subevent.name: Adjust Fatty's feeding amount
subevent.description: After returning home, Yu Xiaowei immediately followed the vet's advice and recalculated Feizai's daily cat food and treat portions, reducing the original amount by about 6% and switching to low-calorie prescription food. At the same time, she used an electronic scale to precisely weigh each meal.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Kowloon City District - home kitchen

subevent.name: Bought a feather wand and started daily interactive play sessions
subevent.description: On her way home, Yu Xiaowei stopped by a pet supply store and bought a feather teaser wand. That afternoon, she used the new teaser wand to play with Feizai for 15 minutes, marking the start of his weight-loss exercise plan.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Kowloon City District - home living room

subevent.name: Record a pet health management memo
subevent.description: Yu Xiaowei recorded in detail in the family memo Feizai's physical examination results that day, vaccination dates, the veterinarian's diet and exercise recommendations, the weight-loss plan she had made, and the daily playtime requirements, so as to continue tracking Feizai's weight changes in the future.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Kowloon City District - Home Study

name: Lin Jiaxin told her that she was about to join the same line of work
description: On November 20, Lin Jiaxin sent a long message that began: "I will officially join a financial advisory firm next month. We may become competitors in the future, but I wanted to tell you first." There was no gratitude, no request for help—only a calm, equal gaze. After reading it, Yu Xiaowei was stunned for a few minutes. Finally she collected herself and replied word by word: "I'm proud of you." She realized that her former dependent best friend had truly become independent.

subevent.name: Lin Jiaxin sent the onboarding notification message.
subevent.description: On November 20, 2025, Yu Xiaowei’s close friend Lin Jiaxin, at her home in Sham Shui Po District, sent Yu Xiaowei a long message via WeChat on her phone, telling her that she would officially join a financial advisory company the following month, becoming a competitor in the same industry as Yu Xiaowei. In the message, Lin Jiaxin expressed her candid attitude and wanted to be the first to tell Yu Xiaowei.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Sham Shui Po District - Lin Jiaxin's home

subevent.name: Yu Xiaowei reads the message and reacts internally
subevent.description: On November 20, 2025, while at her home on Prince Edward Road West in Kowloon City District or during her work commute, Yu Xiaowei received a long message from Lin Jiaxin. After reading it, she was stunned for a few minutes. Her emotions went from surprise to relief, and she sensed that the best friend who had once relied on her was becoming independent. Her feelings were complicated but ultimately turned into comfort.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon City District - Home

subevent.name: Yu Xiaowei replied to the message, expressing her pride.
subevent.description: On November 20, 2025, after her emotions had settled, Yu Xiaowei replied to Lin Jiaxin character by character on WeChat via her phone, writing "Proud of you," expressing respect and encouragement for her best friend's career choice, and wishing her a smooth start in her new job.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon City District - Home

name: Begin creating a Cantonese embroidery work themed on the Year of the Tiger.
description: The praise from the online community inspired Yu Xiaowei, and she decided to carry the success of Peony Painting into a new work. Starting February 17, she began conceiving a Cantonese embroidery piece themed around the Year of the Tiger, combining traditional stitching with the dynamic form of a tiger. Every night after putting the child to sleep, she would sketch under the lamp, select fine silk threads, and embroider bit by bit; this creative work became a quiet harbor in her busy life.

subevent.name: Year of the Tiger theme design and material preparation
subevent.description: At her home in Hong Kong, Yu Xiaowei conceived a Year of the Tiger–themed Guangdong embroidery piece in her study, combining traditional stitching with dynamic tiger poses to draw sketches. She then refined the sketches, annotated the color scheme with colored pencils, and listed the silk threads she would need. Afterwards, she went to the Sham Shui Po fabric market, carefully selected fine, soft silk threads and blended threads, and bought more than 30 colors of embroidery thread. When she got home, she sorted the threads, washed the embroidery fabric, and transferred the sketch onto it, completing the pre-embroidery preparations.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - home study and Sham Shui Po Fabric Market

subevent.name: Conceptualize a Year of the Tiger themed sketch.
subevent.description: In her study at home in Kowloon City District, Hong Kong, Yu Xiaowei spread out drawing paper and pencils and began to conceive a Cantonese embroidery piece with a Year of the Tiger theme. Combining traditional Cantonese embroidery stitch techniques (such as straight stitch, twisted stitch, and seed stitch) with the tiger's dynamic form, she repeatedly sketched the tiger's outline, fur direction, and color gradations, and finally completed a complete design sketch of a tiger in a leaping pose with an auspicious cloud pattern in the background.
subevent.location: Home study in Kowloon City District, Hong Kong.

subevent.name: Refine the sketch and finalize the color scheme
subevent.description: Yu Xiaowei continued to refine yesterday's sketch in her home study, using colored pencils to mark the embroidery thread colors needed for different areas. For example, the tiger's body would use a gradient of orange-yellow, dark brown, and white; the eyes would use emerald green and black; and the auspicious clouds would use royal blue and gold. She listed the color numbers and quantities of the required embroidery threads in her notebook, preparing a checklist for going to the market to buy supplies.
subevent.location: Home study in Kowloon City District, Hong Kong.

subevent.name: Go to Sham Shui Po fabric market to pick silk thread
subevent.description: Yu Xiaowei took the MTR to the Sham Shui Po fabric market, carrying sketches, color cards, and a list. She visited familiar thread stalls door to door, carefully comparing the luster, toughness, and color saturation of different brands of threads. She selected fine, soft silk threads and blended threads, buying threads in more than 30 colors, and chatted with shop owners about popular embroidery color combinations lately.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Sham Shui Po Fabric Market

subevent.name: Organize silk threads and complete pre-embroidery preparations.
subevent.description: After returning home, Yu Xiaowei sorted the newly purchased embroidery threads by color and wound them on thread boards, then checked them one by one against the list. She took out the embroidery hoop, embroidery fabric, and embroidery needles of different sizes, washed and dried the fabric, and transferred the sketch from the tracing paper onto the fabric. In the evening, she neatly arranged all the tools and materials in an embroidery basket in the study, ready to begin the actual embroidery the next day.
subevent.location: Home study in Kowloon City District, Hong Kong.

subevent.name: Making a Tiger Year-themed Cantonese embroidery
subevent.description: After putting her two children to sleep every night, Yu Xiaowei focuses on Cantonese embroidery with a Year of the Tiger theme under the lamp, using traditional stitches to carefully outline the tiger's dynamic form, gradually completing the whole piece and enjoying the tranquility and sense of accomplishment that creation brings.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - home living room or study

subevent.name: Tiger Year Cantonese Embroidery - Drafting and Thread Selection
subevent.description: After putting the two children to bed in the evening, Yu Xiaowei started working on a Tiger Year-themed Cantonese embroidery piece alone under the lamp in the living room. First, she sketched the outline of a tiger on the embroidery fabric with a pencil, then selected silk threads in black, yellow, orange, white, and other colors from her thread box to prepare for the embroidery. She recalled the Cantonese embroidery techniques that Teacher Wu had taught her while refining the details of the sketch, making sure the tiger's proportions and posture were balanced. The whole preparation process took about an hour and a half, and after finishing she neatly put away the embroidery hoop and tools.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Home living room

subevent.name: Year of the Tiger Cantonese embroidery — embroidering the outline of a tiger's head
subevent.description: After putting the children to bed in the evening, Yu Xiaowei continued with Cantonese embroidery in the living room. She began using black silk thread and the rolling-needle stitch to embroider the outline of the tiger's head, including the lines of the eyes, nose, and mouth. Because the tiger's head had many details, she was especially focused, striving for even and delicate stitches. After finishing the outline, she switched to yellow silk thread to fill in parts of the tiger's face, creating a base for the later layers of fur. The work lasted about two hours, and when she finished, she carefully checked the tightness of every stitch.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Home living room

subevent.name: Year of the Tiger Cantonese embroidery - embroidering the tiger's eyes and stripes
subevent.description: After putting the children to bed at night, Yu Xiaowei continued her Year of the Tiger Cantonese embroidery in the living room. She meticulously embroidered the tiger's eyes with white and black silk thread, using stitches in different directions to capture the luster of the eyeballs and the sharpness of the pupils. Then, with dark yellow silk thread, she embroidered the tiger's facial stripes using a random stitch method, making the patterns on the forehead and cheeks vivid and three-dimensional. As she embroidered, she softly played old Cantonese songs, enjoying a rare moment of solitude. This embroidery session lasted about two hours.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Home living room

subevent.name: Year of the Tiger Cantonese Embroidery - Embroidering the Tiger's Body and Limbs
subevent.description: After putting the children to bed at night, Yu Xiaowei continued embroidering under the study lamp. She began embroidering the tiger's torso with orange and yellow silk thread using flat stitch, paying attention to color gradients to create a three-dimensional effect. Then she embroidered the outlines of the tiger's front and hind legs with dark thread, and added a little white silk thread to show the details of the tiger's paws. Midway, her daughter Xinxin got up at night; she gently soothed her and sat back down. She worked about an hour and a half that evening, completing the main base of the tiger's body.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - home study

subevent.name: Year of the Tiger Cantonese embroidery - embroidering the tiger's tail and the background flowers and plants
subevent.description: After putting the children to bed at night, Yu Xiaowei continued her embroidery in the living room. She used black and yellow silk thread to embroider the tiger's tail, using curved stitches to express its dynamic movement. Then she began to embroider the bamboo leaves and flowers in the background, using green silk thread with long and short stitches to outline the bamboo leaves, and then used red silk thread to add a few small flowers, making the picture richer. She remembered Teacher Wu saying that Yue embroidery emphasizes "dense but not messy," so she paid special attention to even stitch density. This session lasted about two hours.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Home living room

subevent.name: Year of the Tiger Cantonese Embroidery - Detail Refinement and Color Adjustment
subevent.description: After putting the children to bed, Yu Xiaowei did detailed refinement work on her Tiger Year Cantonese embroidery in the study. She compared the design draft and added supplementary stitching to the tiger's eyebrows, whiskers, and other fine details, using white silk thread to make each whisker distinct. She also checked the overall color scheme and added a few layers of light yellow silk thread to the tiger's belly for better transitions. She used the seed stitch to embroider the pistils of several small flowers in the background, making the piece more exquisite. The work lasted about an hour and a half, and after finishing, she gently cleaned the embroidered surface with a soft brush.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - home study

subevent.name: Tiger Year Cantonese embroidery - finishing, mounting, and appreciation
subevent.description: After putting the children to bed, Yu Xiaowei did the final finishing touches on the Year of the Tiger Cantonese embroidery in the living room. She inspected the whole piece, trimmed excess threads, and pressed the embroidered surface with a low-temperature iron to smooth it. Then she removed the embroidery from the hoop and carefully placed it into a ready-prepared frame. She looked at the finished work — a majestic yet adorable tiger leaping off the fabric with bamboo leaves swaying in the background — and felt a great sense of accomplishment. name: Incorporating fasting into daily life
description: Since August 18, the 16:8 intermittent fasting method has become part of her daily life. Yu Xiaowei's weight has remained stable, her afternoon energy has improved, and her husband has also proactively adjusted the family dinner time to accommodate it. She regards this as a nutritional management aid alongside her marathon training and plans to continue it long term.

subevent.name: Fasting plan launch and family coordination
subevent.description: On August 18, 2025, Yu Xiaowei officially started the 16:8 intermittent fasting method, keeping her daily eating window within 8 hours (for example, from 10 am to 6 pm) and fasting for the other 16 hours. On that day, she explained the principles and schedule of the fasting method to her husband, Zhang Weiming. Zhang Weiming expressed support and proactively cooperated by moving family dinner from the usual 7 pm to between 5:30 and 6 pm to fit Yu Xiaowei's eating window. Yu Xiaowei explained the specific operation and precautions of the fasting method in detail to her husband in the home kitchen.

subevent.name: Daily execution phase of the fasting regimen
subevent.description: Yu Xiaowei began following the 16:8 intermittent fasting method starting August 18, 2025, eating regularly within a fixed eating window every day and drinking only water or unsweetened beverages during the remaining time. During this period, she paid attention to her body's reactions; her weight remained stable (about 55kg), and her afternoon energy improved compared to before, with no more sluggishness. Her husband Zhang Weiming cooperated by adjusting the dinner time, and the whole family's dinner was moved earlier to between 5:30 and 6:00 pm, keeping the family's eating rhythm consistent. Yu Xiaowei regarded this fasting method as a supplement to her nutritional management outside marathon training, and it did not affect her daily work or social activities; she was able to adjust flexibly at home, in the office, and at group meals outside.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - home and office

Yu Xiaowei had lunch at exactly 12:00 PM (roast meat combo rice with Hong Kong-style milk tea), and had dinner with her family at 5:30 PM (steamed fish and greens prepared by Zhang Weiming). Throughout the day, outside the eating window, she only drank plain water and sugar-free lemon water. The first day went smoothly, with no strong hunger pangs.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Kowloon City District - Home dining room

She discussed her experience with her husband Zhang Weiming during dinner and confirmed that the family dinner time has been completely fixed. For occasional overtime situations, she prepares portable sugar-free drinks in advance to ensure the daily eating window is not moved earlier.
