subevent.location: Hong Kong - Kowloon City District - Pacific Coffee, Prince Edward Road West

subevent.name: Confront the client face-to-face about the client-poaching incident
subevent.description: At exactly 3 p.m., Zhou Minyi arrived at the café and sat down. Yu Xiaowei directly confronted Zhou Minyi about the matter of Shenzhen client Wang Qiming having been signed up by another insurance agent, asking whether Zhou Minyi was aware of it or had obstructed the deal behind the scenes. Zhou Minyi's expression shifted slightly, and she argued that the client had compared several companies on his own and she couldn't control that. Yu Xiaowei did not press further, but both knew the trust had been broken, and the atmosphere was awkward.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Kowloon City District - Pacific Coffee, Prince Edward Road West

name: Mid-Autumn reunion: father was absent again; younger brother directly asked why delaying was not a solution.
description: On October 6, the Mid-Autumn Festival, the family gathered at a restaurant for dinner. Her father was absent again, claiming he had “something to do,” and Yu Xiaowei forced a smile. After the dinner, her younger brother Yu Xiaofeng said to her in private, “Sis, continuing to put off Dad's matter is no solution. Are you afraid of hurting his self-esteem, or of affecting your reputation?” She was left speechless and felt isolated and helpless. The deadlock with her father was especially painful during the holiday.

subevent.name: Mid-Autumn Festival family dinner and father's absence
subevent.description: On the evening of October 6, 2025, the Mid-Autumn Festival, Yu Xiaowei had a family dinner with her mother Chen Meiling, husband Zhang Weiming, son Zhang Zixuan, and daughter Zhang Yuxin in a private room at Fulum Restaurant in Kowloon City. Her younger brother Yu Xiaofeng rushed back to Hong Kong from Shenzhen to join. Her father Yu Guoqiang was absent again, citing that he had matters to attend to. Yu Xiaowei forced a smile, feeling disappointed inside but striving to maintain the festive atmosphere. She dined and moon-gazed with her family, taking care of the children's emotions.
subevent.location: Kowloon City District, Hong Kong - Fulum Restaurant

subevent.name: After the meal, the younger brother bluntly raised the investment conflict
subevent.description: After the Mid-Autumn Festival dinner, Yu Xiaofeng privately stopped Yu Xiaowei near the restaurant and said bluntly: "Sis, dragging things out about Dad is not the solution. Are you afraid of hurting his self-esteem, or afraid of affecting your reputation?" Faced with her younger brother's questioning, Yu Xiaowei was speechless and felt isolated. The deadlock with her father was especially painful amid the festive atmosphere. Afterwards, she walked alone on the street to calm down, then she and her younger brother each went home.
subevent.location: Kowloon City District, Hong Kong - street near Fu Lin Restaurant

name: Start the stress-relief ritual of writing a gratitude journal.
description: On November 3, 2025, due to declining vision and accumulated inner stress, Yu Xiaowei happened to find a blank notebook that a friend had given her years ago and decided to start keeping a paper diary as a way to relieve stress. Every night before bed, she spent 15 minutes using a fountain pen to record three small things she was grateful for, along with her moods or thoughts. Gradually, the diary evolved from a simple log of daily events into deeper self-reflection, such as her guilt over her father's investment incident and her reflections on workplace competition. The act of writing gave her emotions a container, and her insomnia improved slightly, turning it into a fixed bedtime ritual.

subevent.name: Initial gratitude journal habit formation (the running-record stage)
subevent.description: From November 5 to November 10, 2025, Yu Xiaowei persisted in writing a gratitude journal every night before bed, but the content was fairly superficial, mostly specific good things that happened that day, such as smooth work, family gatherings, and good food. She had to deliberately recall to come up with three items, and the writing process remained at the level of recording facts. During this period, she gradually established a nightly writing routine, and the frequency of insomnia decreased slightly.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - home bedroom

subevent.name: Write a gratitude journal the next day
subevent.description: On the evening of November 5, 2025, Yu Xiaowei continued writing her gratitude journal in her bedroom at home before going to sleep. She recalled the good things that happened that day: chatting with her colleague Su Lishan over Hong Kong-style milk tea at a cha chaan teng near the office, helping her son Xuanxuan with homework after work, and receiving a parcel that her husband Zhang Weiming had picked up for her. She wrote down these three things. Although the content was still superficial, she found the process of recalling smoother than on the first day. After writing, she went to bed on time and felt at peace.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - home bedroom

subevent.name: Day 3: Write a gratitude journal
subevent.description: On the evening of November 6, 2025, Yu Xiaowei wrote in her gratitude journal in her bedroom at home before going to sleep. She recalled the day: when she got up in the morning, the sunlight outside the window was lovely; on the way to work she successfully bought a fresh pineapple bun; in the evening the whole family watched a TV show together. She wrote down these specific things, realizing that she had begun to consciously notice the little blessings in daily life. After writing, she felt calm inside, and her insomnia had improved compared with last week.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - home bedroom

subevent.name: Day 6: writing a gratitude journal
subevent.description: On the evening of November 9, 2025, Yu Xiaowei continued writing her gratitude journal in her bedroom at home before going to sleep. She recalled the day: she had a long phone call with her best friend Lin Jiaxin; in the afternoon, she did handmade embroidery at home and finished a small flower pattern; for dinner, her mother Chen Meiling made pork bone soup with green radish and carrot. She recorded these things one by one, and the writing process became increasingly natural, no longer requiring deliberate recall. She felt that this habit was slowly becoming part of her life.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - home bedroom

subevent.name: Write a gratitude journal on the seventh day
subevent.description: On the evening of November 10, 2025, Yu Xiaowei finished the first week of her gratitude journal in her bedroom at home before going to sleep. She recalled the day: she successfully scheduled a meeting with client Wang Qiming for the next week, video-called her younger brother Yu Xiaofeng in the evening and saw his newborn baby, and before bed her daughter Xinxin kissed her cheek and said goodnight. She wrote down these good things; although the style was still a plain log, it had formed a steady rhythm. Over the week, she clearly noticed that her insomnia frequency had decreased and decided to keep going.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - home bedroom

subevent.name: Mid-term journal deepening: shifting toward self-reflection and emotional expression
subevent.description: Starting November 11, 2025, Yu Xiaowei added reflections on her inner feelings to her gratitude journal. She recorded her guilt over her father's investment incident, the pressure of workplace competition, and her worry about her recent decline in vision. Her writing shifted from a daily routine record to deep emotional catharsis. She learned to sort out complex emotions and look for the positive side. During this period, her nightly writing time extended to 20 minutes. She felt that her emotions had a safe outlet, and her insomnia improved even more noticeably.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - home bedroom

subevent.name: Record guilt over father's investment
subevent.description: On the evening of November 11, 2025, while writing in her gratitude journal in her bedroom at home, Yu Xiaowei for the first time shifted the content from a routine log to deep emotional catharsis. She began reflecting on the family financial pressure caused by her father Yu Guoqiang's recent investment mistakes, and wrote in detail about her guilt for failing to remind him in time, as well as her attempt to find positive lessons from the failure. The whole writing process lasted about 20 minutes, and she felt her emotions were safely released.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - home bedroom

subevent.name: Recording the pressure of workplace competition
subevent.description: On the evening of November 14, 2025, Yu Xiaowei continued to deepen her diary writing in her bedroom at home. She focused on recording the pressure of intensifying workplace competition in her current insurance sales job, reflecting on the performance comparison with her colleague Su Lishan, and how to balance client retention and new client development. Through writing, she sorted out complex emotions and tried to find positive strategies to face them. The writing lasted about 20 minutes.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - home bedroom

subevent.name: Recording concerns about deteriorating vision
subevent.description: On the evening of November 17, 2025, Yu Xiaowei wrote in her diary in her bedroom at home, mainly expressing her concern about her recent declining eyesight. She described in detail the eye fatigue caused by long hours of using her phone and computer for work, as well as the blurred vision she experienced after marathon training. In the diary she tried to analyze possible causes and planned to reduce screen time. She wrote for about 20 minutes, and her emotions were soothed.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - home bedroom

subevent.name: Summarized the benefits of the reflective journaling.
subevent.description: On the evening of November 20, 2025, Yu Xiaowei summarized the deepening phase of her mid-term diary in her bedroom at home. She reviewed the 11-day diary-writing process starting November 11, sorted out her emotional changes while recording her guilt toward her father, work pressure, and health concerns, and felt that her insomnia had improved significantly. She wrote down her plans to continue keeping an emotional diary in the future, noted positive gains in her notebook, and spent about 20 minutes writing.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - home bedroom

subevent.name: Reinforcement phase: journaling becomes a fixed ritual
subevent.description: From November 21 to 30, 2025, the gratitude journal had fully become part of Yu Xiaowei's bedtime routine. She no longer needed deliberate reminders; when the time came, she would pick up the journal on her own. The content became richer, including not only small things to be grateful for, but also expectations for the future and affirmation of her own growth. She noticed that her eye strain had eased and she fell asleep more easily at night. Writing in the journal became the most important moment of self-healing in her day.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - home bedroom

subevent.name: Write a gratitude journal every night before bed
subevent.description: Every night before bed (around 10 p.m.), Yu Xiaowei would sit at the desk in her bedroom at home, spontaneously take out her gratitude journal, and write down the small things during the day worth being grateful for, her expectations for the future, and affirmations of her own growth. The process lasted about 15 minutes, after which she closed the journal and went to bed. She found that her eye strain had noticeably eased and she fell asleep more easily at night. Writing in her journal had become the most important moment of self-healing in her day.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - home bedroom

name: Celebrated her husband's birthday at a Chaozhou restaurant; family warmth brought support for the transition.
description: On the evening of October 30, Yu Xiaowei arranged for the whole family and her parents to celebrate her husband Zhang Weiming's birthday at a Teochew restaurant near Prince Edward. She ordered the chilled crab and the marinated meat platter that her husband loved, and in advance she and the children had hand-drawn birthday cards. During the meal, her husband made a wish that the whole family would be healthy. Yu Xiaowei gave him a new fitness band and a pair of running shoes, encouraging him to go jogging together. The warmth of the family sitting together filled the entire private room and provided emotional support for her husband's upcoming career transition. After the meal, Yu Xiaowei quietly sent a photo of her husband making his wish to the family group chat and wrote, 'Ming Zai, we will all be with you.'

subevent.name: Prepare a hand-drawn birthday card and gift
subevent.description: During the day on October 30, Yu Xiaowei hand-drew birthday cards at home with her son Zhang Zixuan and daughter Zhang Yuxin, creating a playful birthday greeting for her husband Zhang Weiming. She had also bought a new fitness band and a pair of running shoes as birthday gifts in advance, carefully wrapped them, and planned to give them to her husband at the evening birthday celebration at a Teochew restaurant.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Kowloon City District - living room at home.

subevent.name: Confirmed the dinner reservation at the Chaozhou restaurant.
subevent.description: On the afternoon of October 30, Yu Xiaowei went to a Teochew restaurant near Prince Edward Road West to confirm the private room reservation for that evening and pre-order dishes her husband liked, such as chilled crab and a marinated platter. She also told the server the specific dining time and number of guests to ensure the dinner went smoothly.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Kowloon City District - Teochew restaurant on Prince Edward Road West

subevent.name: Family dinner at a Chiu Chow restaurant to celebrate a birthday.
subevent.description: On the evening of October 30, Yu Xiaowei, together with her husband Zhang Weiming, son Zhang Zixuan, daughter Zhang Yuxin, her mother Chen Meiling, and her father Yu Guoqiang, went to a private room at a Chaozhou restaurant on Prince Edward Road West to celebrate her husband's birthday. During the meal, the children gave handmade birthday cards, and Yu Xiaowei gifted a new fitness band and running shoes, encouraging her husband to jog together. Zhang Weiming made a wish for the whole family's health. Everyone sat around and enjoyed delicacies such as chilled crab and a marinated meat platter. The warm and harmonious atmosphere provided emotional support for her husband's upcoming career transition.
subevent.location: Private room at a Chiu Chow restaurant on Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

subevent.name: Send birthday photos to the family group
subevent.description: On the evening of October 30, after dinner, Yu Xiaowei quietly took a photo of her husband making a wish in the private room of a Chaozhou restaurant, then sent it via her phone to the family WeChat group with the message “Ming Zai, we are all with you,” thereby expressing her firm support for her husband's career transition and allowing relatives and friends far away or unable to attend to feel the warmth of the family.
subevent.location: Private room at a Chiu Chow restaurant on Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Resumed systematic marathon training; running partner Shen Peiwen joined the joint training and made a periodized plan
description: On the morning of August 1, Yu Xiaowei officially resumed systematic marathon training, with her goal set on breaking 1 hour 55 minutes in the November half marathon. Her running partner Shen Peiwen soon joined the joint training. The two met on the waterfront track on the mornings of August 1 to 3 and jointly developed a 12-week periodized training plan, including interval runs, tempo runs, and long-distance runs. Because of the family trip to Macau from August 4 to 6, training was concentrated before the trip. After the morning run on August 3, the two rested on a bench beside the track. Shen Peiwen talked about the freedom and loneliness of life as an older single female teacher, while Yu Xiaowei reflected on the pressure of juggling multiple roles. Sharing honestly in their sweat, they went from training pace to life pace. After the trip ended on August 7, she resumed training as planned and continued to follow the training schedule.

subevent.name: First morning run of resuming training, invited Shen Peiwen to train together.
subevent.description: At 6 a.m. on August 1, 2025, Yu Xiaowei put on her running gear and set off from her home on Prince Edward Road West in Kowloon City District, Hong Kong, walking to the waterfront track at Kowloon Bay Waterfront Park for her first recovery training after the off-season. Her running partner Shen Peiwen was waiting at the start of the track as promised. After meeting, they did a 15-minute dynamic warm-up, then completed a 5-kilometer easy run at a 5-minute-per-kilometer pace while chatting about recent updates. While resting after the run, Yu Xiaowei took the initiative to invite Shen Peiwen to join her 12-week half-marathon preparation training, and Shen Peiwen readily agreed. The two decided to discuss the framework of the periodized training plan in detail during their next joint session the following day.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon Bay Waterfront Park running track

subevent.name: Develop a 12-week periodized training plan with Shen Peiwen
subevent.description: At 6:00 a.m. on August 2, 2025, Yu Xiaowei and Shen Peiwen continued their joint training on the track at Kowloon Bay Waterfront Park. Today's training was a 6-kilometer tempo run (5:10 per kilometer pace), with the two alternating the lead to maintain the rhythm. After the run, they sat on a bench beside the track, took out their phones and notebooks, and worked together to formulate a 12-week periodized training plan. Shen Peiwen was good at data analysis. Based on Yu Xiaowei's goal of finishing a half marathon in under 1 hour 55 minutes, she planned the specific pace and mileage for each week's interval runs, tempo runs, and long-distance runs. Yu Xiaowei, in turn, incorporating her family and work schedule, fixed the training times to early morning every Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday. The two reached an agreement and synced the plan to their phone calendars. Since Xiaowei would take the whole family to Macau for a trip the following week (August 4-6), they decided to move this week's long-distance run up to August 3.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon Bay Waterfront Park running track

subevent.name: Final day of pre-race intensive training and life sharing
subevent.description: At 6 a.m. on August 3, 2025, Yu Xiaowei and Shen Peiwen carried out their last long run before the trip as planned, completing a 12-kilometer jog on the track at Kowloon Bay Waterfront Park (pace 5:40 per kilometer) as this week's training reserve. After the run, the two rested on a bench by the track and drank water. Shen Peiwen remarked on the freedom and loneliness of being an older single female teacher, while Yu Xiaowei shared the pressure and fulfillment of juggling multiple roles as an insurance agent, mother of two, and running enthusiast. The two talked about the rhythm of training and the rhythm of life, communicating honestly in the sweat and encouraging each other. After the chat, Yu Xiaowei returned home to pack for the Macau family trip departing the next day.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon Bay Waterfront Park running track

subevent.name: After the Macau trip, resumed training and followed the schedule
subevent.description: On the morning of August 7, 2025, after Yu Xiaowei returned to Hong Kong from a family trip to Macau, she resumed training on the track at Kowloon Bay Waterfront Park according to the 12-week periodized training plan previously made with Shen Peiwen. Today's schedule was a 5 km easy run (6 min/km pace) as a recovery run to monitor her physical condition. Yu Xiaowei completed the training on her own and shared the training data in the chat group with Shen Peiwen, preparing for their subsequent joint workouts. After the run, she felt good and decided to continue with the planned interval runs and tempo runs.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon Bay Waterfront Park running track

name: Celebrating mother-in-law's recovery, the whole family gathered for tea and conversation.
description: On the morning of April 29, with her mother-in-law's ankle basically recovered, Yu Xiaowei and her husband Zhang Weiming specially arranged for the whole family to have morning tea at the Dimao Guan Teahouse in Kowloon City. Her parents, children, and mother-in-law all gathered together and ordered traditional dim sum such as char siu buns, shrimp dumplings, and siu mai. During the meal, everyone reviewed the past two weeks of busyness and mutual support. The mother-in-law repeatedly thanked her daughter-in-law for her attentive care, while Yu Xiaowei was grateful for the support of her husband and mother. The children vied to tell funny stories about school, and laughter filled the room. This tea gathering not only celebrated the mother-in-law's recovery but also relaxed the whole family's tense nerves and further strengthened family cohesion.

subevent.name: Preparing for the tea gathering and notifying family.
subevent.description: On the morning of April 29, Yu Xiaowei, at home, notified her husband Zhang Weiming, mother-in-law Li Shufen, parents Chen Meiling and Yu Guoqiang, and her two children Zhang Zixuan and Zhang Yuxin by phone and in person, confirming the family dim sum gathering at De Mao Guan Teahouse in Kowloon City that morning, and reminded everyone to leave on time. Afterwards, she briefly tidied her personal belongings and got ready to go out.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon City District - 328 Prince Edward Road West

subevent.name: The whole family went to the teahouse
subevent.description: On the morning of April 29, Yu Xiaowei set off from home with her husband Zhang Weiming, son Zhang Zixuan, daughter Zhang Yuxin, mother Chen Meiling, father Yu Guoqiang, and mother-in-law Li Shufen. They walked or took short-distance transport to the Dimao Guan Teahouse in Kowloon City, a trip of about fifteen minutes. The family chatted happily along the way, and the mood was relaxed and cheerful.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon City District - on the way from Prince Edward Road West to Di Mao Guan Teahouse

subevent.name: Enjoying dim sum at a teahouse to celebrate her mother-in-law's recovery.
subevent.description: The whole family gathered at Dimaoguan Teahouse in Kowloon City and ordered traditional dim sum such as barbecue pork buns, shrimp dumplings, and siu mai. During the meal, Yu Xiaowei and her husband Zhang Weiming reviewed the family's busyness and mutual support over the past two weeks while her mother-in-law was recovering from an ankle injury. Her mother-in-law, Li Shuzhen (actually Li Shufen), repeatedly thanked Yu Xiaowei for her attentive care, while Yu Xiaowei expressed gratitude for the support from her husband and parents. The children Zhang Zixuan and Zhang Yuxin competed to tell amusing stories from school, and laughter filled the room. The tea gathering lasted about two hours in a warm and harmonious atmosphere, further strengthening family cohesion.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon City District - Di Mao Guan Teahouse

name: Couples' low-calorie home cooking workshop
description: On October 11, Yu Xiaowei and her husband attended a “Low-Calorie Home Cooking” workshop at the community center. Together they made salmon avocado salad, quinoa rice balls, and tofu cheesecake. Her husband was skilled with the knife, and she was in charge of plating. After the class, they agreed to cook one new dish together each month to support her weight management. That evening, they tried making quinoa rice balls, which were well received by the children.

subevent.name: Go to the community center to attend a cooking workshop
subevent.description: On the morning of October 11, Yu Xiaowei and her husband Zhang Weiming went to the community activity center in Kowloon City District, Hong Kong, to attend the Low-Calorie Home Cooking workshop organized by the community center.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Kowloon City District - Community Activity Centre

subevent.name: Learning and making low-calorie family dishes at a workshop
subevent.description: In the workshop, Yu Xiaowei and her husband Zhang Weiming completed three low-calorie dishes together: salmon avocado salad, quinoa rice balls, and tofu cheesecake. Her husband handled the cutting and preparation of ingredients, while Yu Xiaowei handled plating and decoration. The two worked well together and learned low-calorie cooking techniques.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Kowloon City District - Community Activity Centre Kitchen

subevent.name: Agreed after class to explore healthy recipes together.
subevent.description: After the workshop, Yu Xiaowei and her husband Zhang Weiming agreed to cook one new dish together every month, to support Yu Xiaowei's weight management plan, enhance spousal cooperation, and promote healthy family eating.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Kowloon City District - Community Activity Centre

subevent.name: That evening, she recreated the quinoa rice balls at home and the kids loved them.
subevent.description: That evening, Yu Xiaowei and her husband Zhang Weiming made the quinoa rice balls they had learned in the workshop again in their home kitchen, and let their two children Zhang Zixuan and Zhang Yuxin taste them. The children really liked them and gave positive reviews, and the family enjoyed a healthy dinner.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Kowloon City District - home kitchen

name: Collected year-end bonus and planned its allocation.
description: On December 10, Yu Xiaowei received her year-end bonus and December salary from the company, totaling about 58,000 yuan. She deposited 20,000 yuan into the family emergency reserve account, used 10,000 yuan to pay the remaining balance for the massage chair, and planned to use the rest for her daughter's ballet class renewal and her son's interest class fees. She recorded the income in detail in her mobile bookkeeping app and reminded her husband, Zhang Weiming, to pay attention to family cash flow.

subevent.name: Receive year-end bonus and December salary
subevent.description: On December 10, 2025, Yu Xiaowei received her year-end bonus and December salary at the AIA Hong Kong office, totaling approximately 58,000 yuan, and confirmed the income via a bank account notification.
subevent.location: AIA Building office, Wan Chai District, Hong Kong

subevent.name: Deposit 20,000 yuan into the family emergency reserve fund.
subevent.description: At the office, Yu Xiaowei used the mobile banking app to transfer 20,000 yuan from her salary account to the dedicated family emergency reserve account, completing the deposit.
subevent.location: AIA Building office, Wan Chai District, Hong Kong

subevent.name: Pay the balance of 10,000 yuan for the massage chair.
subevent.description: Yu Xiaowei used mobile banking to transfer 10,000 yuan to the massage chair vendor, settling the remaining balance for the massage chair purchased earlier, and received a merchant confirmation notification.
subevent.location: AIA Building office, Wan Chai District, Hong Kong

subevent.name: Record income distribution details in the expense-tracking app
subevent.description: Yu Xiaowei recorded the day's income (year-end bonus and December salary) and various expenses/transfers (deposited 20,000 into the emergency reserve, paid the 10,000 balance for the massage chair) in her mobile expense-tracking app, and noted that the remaining funds were planned for her daughter's ballet class renewal and her son's interest class fees.
subevent.location: AIA Building office, Wan Chai District, Hong Kong

subevent.name: Remind husband to keep an eye on the family cash flow.
subevent.description: After finishing her bookkeeping, Yu Xiaowei contacted her husband Zhang Weiming via a WeChat voice call to tell him about the year-end bonus distribution and remind him to keep an eye on other recent household expenses to ensure healthy cash flow.
subevent.location: AIA Building office, Wan Chai District, Hong Kong

name: Husband comforted her late at night, and the couple worked together through the difficulty
description: On the evening of October 10, Yu Xiaowei tossed and turned, unable to sleep because her Shenzhen client had been poached and because of the conflict over her father's investment. Her husband Zhang Weiming noticed, made two cups of warm milk, and sat on the edge of the bed to ask her softly. Yu Xiaowei finally let down her guard and told him everything about Zhou Minyi's betrayal and her father's stubbornness. Zhang Weiming held her hand and said, 'No matter what happens outside, there will always be someone at home supporting you.' They talked into the early morning, and Yu Xiaowei felt a rare sense of peace. Their relationship grew even closer in this vulnerable moment.

subevent.name: Yu Xiaowei tossed and turned, unable to sleep because of the conflict during the day
subevent.description: On the night of October 10, Yu Xiaowei lay in bed, her mind repeatedly replaying the client being poached during the day and the conflict over her father's investment. She felt anxious and wronged, could not fall asleep, but did not want to disturb her family, so she tossed and turned alone.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon City District - home bedroom

subevent.name: Husband and wife have a late-night heart-to-heart.
subevent.description: With her husband's patient companionship, Yu Xiaowei finally let down her guard and poured out everything about Zhou Minyi's betrayal in stealing clients and her father's stubborn insistence on investing. Zhang Weiming held her hand and comforted her: ‘No matter what happens outside, there will always be someone at home supporting you.’ The two talked until the early morning, and Yu Xiaowei felt a long-lost sense of security.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon City District - home bedroom

subevent.name: The couple reconciled and fell asleep peacefully
subevent.description: After a long late-night talk, Yu Xiaowei's emotions were calmed, and the couple's relationship grew even closer in a vulnerable moment. The two fell asleep in each other's arms, and Yu Xiaowei finally let go of her psychological burden and slept peacefully.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon City District - home bedroom

name: Held an introductory Cantonese embroidery sharing class, received the studio key, and started the rush plan to finish the 'Winter' embroidery piece.
description: On December 7, 2025, Yu Xiaowei and He Meiling successfully held the first "Cantonese Embroidery Introductory Sharing Class" at the Kowloon City District Community Centre. In the morning they prepared the venue; in the afternoon the class was officially taught. Teacher Wu Xiuying attended and formally handed over the studio key to Yu Xiaowei. During her speech, Yu's voice choked up, but she did not mention her family difficulties. After class, Teacher Wu suggested signing up for the Hong Kong Traditional Crafts Exhibition in March 2026 and urged her to finish the "Winter" embroidery piece. Yu Xiaowei made a solemn promise. Starting December 8, she drew up a detailed catch-up plan and spent her spare time every day intensively on the embroidery.

subevent.name: Preparing a Cantonese embroidery introductory sharing class
subevent.description: On the morning of December 7, 2025, Yu Xiaowei and He Meiling set up the teaching venue at a community center in Kowloon City District. They prepared the embroidery material kits, display stands, tables and chairs, debugged the audio and projection equipment, and coordinated with community staff for a final check to ensure the afternoon sharing class could run smoothly.
subevent.location: Hong Kong-Kowloon City District Community Centre

subevent.name: Host an introductory Cantonese embroidery sharing session and receive the studio key
subevent.description: On the afternoon of December 7, 2025, Yu Xiaowei and He Meiling officially hosted the first "Cantonese Embroidery Introductory Sharing Class" at the community center in Kowloon City District. They taught about 20 participants the history of Cantonese embroidery and basic stitching, and demonstrated simple pattern embroidery on site. During the class, Teacher Wu Xiuying attended and formally handed over the studio key to Yu Xiaowei. Yu Xiaowei's voice choked up during her speech as she thanked Teacher Wu for her trust, but she did not mention her family difficulties.
subevent.location: Hong Kong-Kowloon City District Community Centre

subevent.name: Discuss craft exhibition registration and promise to rush the work
subevent.description: After class on the afternoon of December 7, 2025, Yu Xiaowei had a private conversation with Teacher Wu Xiuying in the rest area of the community center. Teacher Wu suggested that Yu Xiaowei register for the Hong Kong Traditional Craft Exhibition in March 2026 and urged her to finish the "Winter" embroidery piece as soon as possible. Yu Xiaowei solemnly promised to step up her work, noted the registration deadline and artwork submission requirements on the spot, and then discussed the general exhibition layout concept with Teacher Wu.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - community center rest area in Kowloon City District

subevent.name: Started the accelerated finishing plan for the "Winter" embroidery piece
subevent.description: Starting from December 8, 2025, Yu Xiaowei used her after-work and weekend time every day to intensively embroider the "Winter" embroidery piece in her home study. She re-planned her embroidery schedule, focusing on embroidery for at least 2 hours per day, and planned to complete the main part within two months, reserving one month for adjustments and framing, in order to submit the complete work before the March 2026 craft exhibition.
subevent.location: Home study in Kowloon City District, Hong Kong.

name: Hong Kong Street Marathon full-marathon debut
description: On the morning of October 26, Yu Xiaowei took on her first full marathon of 42.195 kilometers in her life. Her pace was steady for the first 25 kilometers, but after 30 kilometers severe leg cramps forced her to walk. She finished in 5 hours and 28 minutes. Her husband and children were waiting at the finish line, and her daughter hugged her. That evening she shared in the running group: 'A full marathon is like life — only after falling apart do you realize how much you can endure.'

subevent.name: Getting up in the early morning and pre-race preparation
subevent.description: At 4 a.m. on October 26, Yu Xiaowei got up, washed up, changed into her running gear, and checked and put on her race bib, running shoes, energy gels, and sports watch. She did 15 minutes of dynamic stretching and activation exercises in the living room at home, then drank a glass of warm water and ate a banana as a simple breakfast. After confirming she had her water bottle and phone with her, Yu Xiaowei left her home on Prince Edward Road West, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong at 5 a.m. and took a taxi to the starting point of the Hong Kong Streetathon, the Western Harbour Crossing Kowloon Toll Plaza.
subevent.location: Hong Kong, Kowloon City District - home and the Western Harbour Crossing Kowloon Toll Plaza

subevent.name: Full marathon race process (first 25 km)
subevent.description: At 5:30 a.m., Yu Xiaowei arrived at the start area at the Kowloon Toll Plaza of the Western Harbour Crossing. After storing her bag, she warmed up again and exchanged encouragement with nearby runners. At 6:00 sharp, the full marathon group started with a gun. Following the pacing plan set by Coach Zhao Zhiming, she ran at a steady pace of about 6:10 per kilometer, passing landmarks such as the Western Harbour Crossing, Central waterfront, and Wan Chai Convention and Exhibition Centre. Encouraged by her fellow runner Shen Peiwen, who ran alongside her, she passed the halfway point at around 8:45 a.m., felt good, and maintained her pace until the 25 km mark (around 9:20 a.m.).
subevent.location: Hong Kong Marathon course: Western Harbour Crossing to the northern shore of Hong Kong Island

subevent.name: Full Marathon Race Process (Late-Race Collapse and Persevering to Finish)
subevent.description: At 9:20 a.m., Yu Xiaowei passed the 25-kilometer mark and entered the racecourse around Sham Shui Po and Mong Kok. At about the 30-kilometer mark (9:50 a.m.), a sudden severe cramp hit the back of her thigh, forcing her to stop and walk. She tried stretching and replenishing electrolytes, but the cramp kept recurring, so she could only struggle forward with a run-walk strategy. Despite intense physical pain, Yu Xiaowei persevered with tenacious willpower. Eventually, under the attention of the race sweep vehicle and medical volunteers, she crossed the finish line at Victoria Park at 11:28 a.m., finishing in 5 hours 28 minutes. After crossing the line, she received her finisher medal and was helped by volunteers to the recovery area.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Sham Shui Po, Mong Kok to Victoria Park course

subevent.name: At the finish line, reunited with the family to celebrate.
subevent.description: At 11:40 a.m., after a brief rest in the rest area of Victoria Park, Yu Xiaowei saw her husband Zhang Weiming, son Zhang Zixuan, and daughter Zhang Yuxin waiting at the finish line. Zhang Weiming handed her water and a towel. Zhang Zixuan cheered for his mother with a small flag, and little daughter Zhang Yuxin hugged Yu Xiaowei tightly and said, “Mom, you’re awesome!” The family took a group photo at the finish line. Zhang Weiming had prepared in advance Yu Xiaowei’s favorite pineapple buns with butter and Hong Kong-style milk tea. Yu Xiaowei rested and shared her race experience with her family, and then they all took the MTR home together.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Victoria Park - Finish Area

subevent.name: Post-race recovery and sharing with the running group
subevent.description: At 2 pm, Yu Xiaowei went home, took a cold shower, did some simple stretching to relax, and ate wonton noodles prepared by her mother Chen Meiling to regain energy. She then lay on the sofa to let her legs rest and looked at the official race photos. At 8 pm, she sat in the living room, opened her phone, and posted a message in the Hong Kong Street Marathon running group (including coach Zhao Zhiming, fellow runner Shen Peiwen, etc.) sharing her first marathon experience: “A full marathon is like life; only after you break down do you realize you can hold on.” She also attached a photo of crossing the finish line and a picture of her finisher's medal. People in the group gave likes and encouragement, and Shen Peiwen also shared a composite photo of the two of them running together. Yu Xiaowei replied to everyone's congratulations and went to bed before 10 pm.
subevent.location: Hong Kong, Kowloon City District - living room at home

name: Training conflicts with her daughter's ballet rehearsal; the whole family finds warmth again at a sweet soup shop.
description: On the morning of Saturday, August 9, her daughter's ballet class rehearsal clashed with Yu Xiaowei's long-distance training time. Her husband Zhang Weiming took the initiative to take their daughter to the rehearsal, while Yu Xiaowei finished her training alone and then rushed to the community pool to join her family. As the family picnicked by the pool, she, utterly exhausted, leaned against her backpack and nearly fell asleep. In a daze, she dreamed she was standing alone on an empty marathon course. When she woke, she stared at the children splashing in the water, and a sharp question rose in her heart: 'Am I working this hard really for their good? Or am I afraid to stop, afraid that I would be replaced the moment I do?' She buried the question deep in her heart. That evening, the family of four went to the time-honored dessert shop downstairs. The children chattered about the fun moments from the day's rehearsal, and her husband quietly ordered her favorite glutinous rice balls in ginger soup. In the warm steam, she looked at her family and suddenly felt a kind of 'happiness of wasting time,' and her anxiety briefly melted away.

subevent.name: Morning family conflict negotiation
subevent.description: On Saturday morning, August 9, 2025, at about 7:30, Yu Xiaowei discussed the day's schedule with her husband Zhang Weiming in the living room of their home. Their daughter Zhang Yuxin's ballet class rehearsal was scheduled for 9 a.m., and Yu Xiaowei's own planned long-distance training also had to be done in the morning. After a brief discussion, they decided: Zhang Weiming would take their daughter to the rehearsal and look after their son Zhang Zixuan; Yu Xiaowei would go out alone to complete her training, and afterward the whole family would meet at Kowloon City Swimming Pool for a picnic.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Kowloon City District - 328 Prince Edward Road West, home living room

subevent.name: Morning long-distance marathon training
subevent.description: On the morning of August 9, 2025, from about 8:30 to 10:30, Yu Xiaowei went alone to the running track at Kowloon Tsai Park, not far from home, for long-distance endurance training. Following the plan made by coach Zhao Zhiming, she completed about 15 kilometers of jogging at a pace of 6 minutes 30 seconds per kilometer. During the training, she kept adjusting her breathing and rhythm, briefly replenishing water at the park's water point, and stayed focused throughout. After the training, she did some simple stretching and then walked to Kowloon City Swimming Pool to meet her family.
subevent.location: Hong Kong – Kowloon Tsai Park running track.

subevent.name: Husband took his daughter to ballet rehearsal
subevent.description: At about 8:50 a.m. on August 9, 2025, her husband Zhang Weiming set out from home with their daughter Zhang Yuxin and son Zhang Zixuan and walked to the community arts center in Kowloon City District. From 9:00 to 10:00, Zhang Yuxin attended a rehearsal for her ballet class, while Zhang Weiming and his son waited in the audience area. After the rehearsal, Zhang Weiming helped his daughter pack up her dance shoes and props. The three went on to Kowloon City Swimming Pool at around 10:15, secured a shady spot in the family rest area beside the pool, laid out a picnic mat, and waited for Yu Xiaowei to arrive.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Kowloon City District Community Arts Centre (Ballet Studio)

subevent.name: After training, meet up with family at the pool and have a picnic
subevent.description: At about 10:45 a.m. on August 9, 2025, after finishing training, Yu Xiaowei walked to Kowloon City Swimming Pool and met up with her husband and children. The family of four spread a picnic blanket in the family rest area by the pool and shared the sandwiches, fruit, and drinks they had prepared earlier. The children changed into swimsuits and played in the shallow end, while Yu Xiaowei and Zhang Weiming sat on the blanket and chatted. Because of the extreme fatigue from the high-intensity morning training, Yu Xiaowei leaned against her backpack and quickly fell asleep after eating, for about 20 minutes. In a daze, she dreamed that she was standing alone on an empty marathon course, feeling lonely and lost. When she woke up, she watched the children playing in the water, and a sharp question surfaced in her mind: was she really pushing herself this hard for their sake, or was she afraid to stop, afraid that once she stopped she would be replaced? But she did not reveal this anxiety and quietly continued the picnic with her family.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - family rest area next to Kowloon City Swimming Pool

subevent.name: Warm family time at the sweet soup shop in the evening
subevent.description: At about 7:30 p.m. on August 9, 2025, Yu Xiaowei and her family of four walked from home to Jiajia Dessert Shop on Prince Edward Road West downstairs. The children excitedly shared stories about the day's ballet rehearsal and swimming. Zhang Weiming quietly ordered a bowl of her favorite ginger-syrup glutinous rice balls for Yu Xiaowei. The shop was filled with steam, and the family sat around the table. Looking at her family chatting and laughing, Yu Xiaowei felt her inner anxiety and doubts temporarily melt away, and she felt a kind of 'happiness of wasting time.' She realized that family warmth was the force that kept her going. At about 8:30, the family of four paid the bill and went home, ending a full yet conflicted day.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Kowloon City District, Jiajia Sweet Soup Shop on Prince Edward Road West

name: Sprinted for quarterly performance and signed deals but lost prospective clients; after reflection, strengthened the resolve to study for the CFP.
description: From April 7 to 10, Yu Xiaowei made a full sprint toward her Q2 performance targets and successfully renewed medical insurance policies with two long-time clients. However, a prospective client, Mr. Chen, a small and medium-sized business owner she had been carefully following for nearly half a year, felt that the comprehensive family financial plan Yu Xiaowei provided was not persuasive enough after comparing final proposals, and turned to a competitor. On the evening of April 10, Yu Xiaowei dejectedly confided in her husband Zhang Weiming, attributing the loss to her lack of knowledge in multi-dimensional financial planning and feeling even more strongly the urgency of the investment planning module in the CFP course. That night, she readjusted her study plan, increasing her scheduled weekly CFP online course from four hours to six hours, determined to accelerate her professional improvement.

subevent.name: Start the quarterly performance sprint and contact existing and prospective clients
subevent.description: On Monday, April 7, Yu Xiaowei started her second-quarter performance sprint at the AIA Building office in Wan Chai District, Hong Kong. She first called existing clients Chen Meiling and Li Weiqiang to discuss medical insurance policy renewals and confirm specific terms. Then she called Chen Zhiqiang, a prospective client she had been following up with for nearly six months, to ask about his final intention regarding the family comprehensive financial plan, and agreed to send supplementary materials the next day.
subevent.location: Office at AIA Building, Wan Chai District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

subevent.name: Prepare renewal plan and comparison materials for prospective clients.
subevent.description: At the AIA Building office, Yu Xiaowei organized the renewal documents for two long-standing clients, ensuring the medical insurance policy terms were correct. At the same time, for prospective client Chen Zhiqiang's comprehensive family financial planning needs, she repeatedly calculated the return simulation data for the investment planning module and prepared a comparison table with competitors' plans, trying to highlight her advantage in family risk protection. However, she realized that she lacked knowledge in the investment planning dimension.
subevent.location: Office at AIA Building, Wan Chai District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

subevent.name: Successfully renewed medical insurance policies for two long-term clients
subevent.description: In the afternoon, Yu Xiaowei went to the home of long-time client Chen Meiling in Kowloon City District to complete the renewal of her family medical insurance policy in person, and gave a small gift to thank her for her continued support. She then completed another renewal online with long-time client Li Weiqiang through the electronic signature system. The communication went smoothly throughout, and both policies were successfully locked in, contributing about 20,000 yuan in commission to the quarterly performance.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon City District - Chen Meiling's home and online

subevent.name: Prospective client Chen Zhiqiang was lost to a competitor.
subevent.description: In the morning, Yu Xiaowei received a call from prospective client Chen Zhiqiang in her office. He said clearly that, after comparing her plan with another company's, he thought the comprehensive family financial plan Yu Xiaowei provided lacked professional depth and data support in the investment planning module, and he ultimately chose a competitor's services. Yu Xiaowei politely thanked him on the phone and briefly tried to keep his business, but failed. She realized that her lack of CFP knowledge was the root cause.
subevent.location: Office at AIA Building, Wan Chai District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

subevent.name: Confided her frustrations to her husband and adjusted the CFP study plan.
subevent.description: In the evening, Yu Xiaowei returned home in Kowloon City District, feeling dejected. She told her husband Zhang Weiming in detail on the living room sofa about the loss of the client, attributing it to her lack of knowledge in investment planning. Zhang Weiming patiently comforted her and encouraged her to focus on improvement. Then Yu Xiaowei turned on her computer, replanned her CFP online course schedule, increasing the original four hours per week of study to six hours, and breaking it down into specific tasks for the investment planning module from 8-9 PM each night, determined to accelerate her professional growth.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon City District - living room at home

subevent.name: Execute the new study plan, increasing study time for the first time.
subevent.description: After returning home from work, Yu Xiaowei opened the CFP investment planning module online course video in her study from 8:00 p.m. to 9:30 p.m. according to the adjusted study plan, focusing on studying for 1.5 hours total, and took course notes on customer churn cases, marking key content such as portfolio construction and risk assessment. She planned to continue studying the next day to ensure reaching the weekly target of 6 total study hours.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon City District - Home Study

name: Hold a small Cantonese embroidery charity sale.
description: From December 12 to 15, Yu Xiaowei and He Meiling prepared and held a small Cantonese embroidery charity sale. On December 12, Yu Xiaowei organized the works at home, checked the mounting, made price tags and posters, and communicated the process with He Meiling via WeChat. On Saturday, December 13, they exhibited and sold dozens of Cantonese embroidery works at the Kowloon City District community center, including Peony Painting and Daughter's World: Spring, attracting many neighbors. An elderly overseas Chinese bought Peony Painting at a high price. Teacher Wu Xiuying came to support and encouraged them, saying that only when craftsmanship has warmth can it be passed down. On Monday, December 15, Yu Xiaowei donated all the proceeds to the Hong Kong Children's Cancer Foundation and completed the donation in the name of the three of them. The charity sale promoted Cantonese embroidery and also gave Yu Xiaowei the satisfaction of giving back to society through her interests.

subevent.name: Organizing artwork and preparing supplies before the charity sale
subevent.description: Yu Xiaowei, in her home study and at her home in Wan Chai District on Hong Kong Island, did the final cleaning and framing checks on several completed Cantonese embroidery works (including 'Peony' and 'Daughter's World: Spring'), and made charity sale price tags and promotional posters. At the same time, she communicated with He Meiling via WeChat about the next day's charity sale process, confirming the list of works and charity sale supplies (change box, display stands, etc.) that both parties would bring.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon City District - Home Study

subevent.name: Cantonese embroidery charity sale event at the community center
subevent.description: Yu Xiaowei and He Meiling rented a venue at the Kowloon City District community center. Starting at 9 a.m. they set up the exhibition booth, displaying and selling dozens of Cantonese embroidery works made by themselves and their teacher Wu Xiuying. Many neighbors were attracted to stop and admire the works. Yu Xiaowei introduced the creative inspiration and Cantonese embroidery techniques behind each piece to the visitors. An elderly overseas Chinese was amazed by the beauty of the Peony Picture and bought it at a high price as a collection. Teacher Wu Xiuying came to show support in person and said to Yu Xiaowei emotionally, "Only when craftsmanship carries warmth can it be passed down." The charity sale lasted until 5 p.m., with 25 pieces sold in total.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon City District - Community Centre Activity Room

subevent.name: Donation of charity sale proceeds and follow-up feedback
subevent.description: On Monday morning, Yu Xiaowei went to the Hong Kong Children's Cancer Foundation office and donated all the proceeds from this small Cantonese embroidery charity sale (including the payment from the elderly overseas Chinese who bought 'Peony Painting') in the names of 'Yu Xiaowei, He Meiling, and Wu Xiuying'. She completed the donation procedures on site and received a receipt and a thank-you letter. Afterwards, she told He Meiling and Wu Xiuying in their three-person WeChat group that the donation was complete, and planned to share this good deed on social media to encourage more people to pay attention to the combination of traditional crafts and public welfare.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Central and Western District - Hong Kong Children's Cancer Foundation Office

name: Finished the Standard Chartered Hong Kong Half Marathon with a sub-2 time.
description: On January 4, Yu Xiaowei went to Victoria Park to pick up race materials and consulted her coach about pacing strategy. On January 5, she got up early and took part in the Standard Chartered Hong Kong Half Marathon, finishing in 1 hour 58 minutes, successfully breaking 2 hours. Her family came to cheer her on and reunited at the finish line. After the race, client Wang Qiming left a message mentioning the cross-border insurance sharing session, planting a seed for business. In the evening, she celebrated with her family.

subevent.name: Pre-race preparation
subevent.description: Yu Xiaowei went to the designated race pack pickup point for the Standard Chartered Hong Kong Marathon (Victoria Park), collected her race pack, including the race bib, timing chip, event T-shirt, etc., and carefully checked her personal running gear (running shoes, sportswear, energy gels, sports watch). She then asked her coach Zhao Zhiming for final training advice via WhatsApp, confirmed the pacing strategy for the day, and made sure everything was ready.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Victoria Park

subevent.name: Race day: get up early and set off
subevent.description: At 5 a.m., Yu Xiaowei got up, had a pre-race breakfast (banana, whole-wheat bread, a little Hong Kong-style milk tea), put on race gear, checked her belongings, confirmed the family meeting point with her husband Zhang Weiming on the phone, then took the MTR alone from her home in Kowloon City District to the starting area in Tsim Sha Tsui.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Home in Kowloon City District to Tsim Sha Tsui MTR Station.

subevent.name: Pre-race warm-up and gathering at the start
subevent.description: Yu Xiaowei arrived at the Tsim Sha Tsui start area at 6:30, did a light jog and dynamic stretching in the designated warm-up zone, and met fellow runner Shen Peiwen. They encouraged each other and took a photo together. She then entered the start corral according to her pace zone and waited for the 7:00 starting gun.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Tsim Sha Tsui - Standard Chartered Marathon start area

subevent.name: Half-marathon final sprint
subevent.description: After the 7:00 start, Yu Xiaowei advanced steadily according to the planned pace strategy. Along the Kowloon Bay course section, she saw her husband Zhang Weiming and their children holding cheer signs and shouting. She crossed the finish line at Victoria Park in 1 hour and 58 minutes, successfully achieving the sub-2 goal, and received the finisher medal.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Standard Chartered Marathon course (Tsim Sha Tsui to Victoria Park)

subevent.name: Reunion with family at the finish line
subevent.description: After crossing the finish line and collecting her finisher supplies, Yu Xiaowei met her family in the family waiting area at the Victoria Park finish zone. Her mother Chen Meiling, father Yu Guoqiang, husband Zhang Weiming, son Zhang Zixuan, and daughter Zhang Yuxin were all there to congratulate her. Her daughter Zhang Yuxin gave her a hug, and her father Yu Guoqiang praised her. The family took a group photo on a park bench and chatted about the race details.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Victoria Park finish area

subevent.name: Reply to customer messages and follow up on business opportunities.
subevent.description: During the rest after the competition, Yu Xiaowei checked WeChat on her phone and saw a congratulatory message from her client Wang Qiming, who also mentioned, 'There is a cross-border insurance sharing session in Shenzhen in March; drop by if you have time.' Yu Xiaowei immediately replied with thanks, expressed great interest in the cross-border insurance sharing, and arranged a time to discuss it in detail later, preparing for potential business development.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Victoria Park

subevent.name: Post-race recovery and family celebration
subevent.description: Yu Xiaowei returned by car with her family to their home in Kowloon City District, where she applied ice, stretched to relax, and replenished protein and fluids. Then she showered and changed clothes, and had lunch with her family at a nearby restaurant to celebrate. In the afternoon, she rested at home, sorted through race photos, posted a race-completion update on social media, and called her close friend Lin Jiaxin to share the joy.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - at home and a nearby restaurant in Kowloon City District.

name: Team quarterly performance review and formulation and submission of reform proposals
description: From September 28 to 29, 2025, Yu Xiaowei and Su Lishan worked together in a meeting room at the AIA Building in Hong Kong to organize Q3 performance data, tally the number of policy signings, customer feedback, and satisfaction scores. After confirming the effect of the reform, Yu Xiaowei drafted the Q4 Team Incentives and Task Allocation Optimization Proposal. At the team meeting on October 2, Yu Xiaowei formally submitted the proposal and led a discussion, soliciting team feedback to further refine the plan.

subevent.name: Consolidate the data and draft optimization recommendations.
subevent.description: On September 29, 2025, Yu Xiaowei and Su Lishan continued their work review in the AIA Hong Kong meeting room, summarizing each member's number of policy signings, customer feedback, and satisfaction scores. Based on confirmation of the reform's effectiveness, Yu Xiaowei drafted a proposal titled Q4 Team Incentive and Work Allocation Optimization Recommendations, covering group incentive plans and adjustments to mentoring responsibilities for new staff, and planned to submit it for discussion at the team meeting in early October.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Wan Chai District - Meeting room, AIA Building, 138 Gloucester Road

subevent.name: Submit optimization suggestions at the team meeting in early October.
subevent.description: On October 2, 2025 (the team's regular meeting day in early October), Yu Xiaowei formally submitted the Q4 Team Incentive and Division of Work Optimization Proposal drafted by herself to team members in the AIA Hong Kong Tower conference room, explained and discussed the proposal contents, and sought team feedback to further refine the plan.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Wan Chai District - Meeting room, AIA Building, 138 Gloucester Road

name: Start building a long-term eye-care habit.
description: After getting fitted for glasses, Yu Xiaowei strictly followed habits such as limiting screen use, reading under an eye-protection desk lamp, and relaxing with morning eye yoga. By the end of the year, she felt that her symptoms of dry and irritated eyes had significantly eased, and she regularly recommended eye-care methods to her colleagues.

subevent.name: Eye-care habit implementation and evaluation
subevent.description: Starting July 12, 2025, Yu Xiaowei began a daily eye-care routine in her home study, including using an eye-protection desk lamp, resting and looking into the distance every 45 minutes, and doing eye yoga in the morning and evening. During this period, she conducted multiple weekend self-assessments of eye fatigue (the known second one was on September 14, the third on October 12, and the fifth on December 28), and finally completed a habit summary on December 30, forming a stable biological rhythm.
subevent.location: Hong Kong, Kowloon City District - home study

subevent.name: Start implementing eye care habits.
subevent.description: At her home study in Kowloon City District, Yu Xiaowei officially started her daily eye-care routine: she turned on the eye-protection desk lamp whenever working or using screens throughout the day, and after every 45 consecutive minutes of screen time, she stood up and looked out the window for 5 minutes. In the morning after getting up and at night before going to bed, she did 5 minutes of eye yoga, including eye rolling, focus training, and acupressure massage around the eyes. She fully completed all the steps that day and recorded her initial eye fatigue level as moderate.
subevent.location: Hong Kong, Kowloon City District - home study

subevent.name: Carry out the eye-care habit and do the second weekend assessment
subevent.description: Yu Xiaowei has continued to implement eye-care habits at home: the eye-protection desk lamp remains on during all working hours, she takes a break every 45 minutes to rest and look into the distance, and morning and evening eye yoga have become a biological routine. On the weekend, she conducted her second self-assessment of eye fatigue. Compared with last month's data, she found that fatigue had decreased further, and she could naturally trigger rest reminders without having to deliberately time them.
subevent.location: Hong Kong, Kowloon City District - home study

subevent.name: Follow the eye-care habit and do the third weekend assessment
subevent.description: At home, Yu Xiaowei smoothly followed her daily eye-care routine: turning on the eye-protective desk lamp, taking a 5-minute break after every 45 minutes of work, and doing eye yoga morning and evening had become part of her daily rhythm. The third weekend assessment showed her eye strain had dropped to a mild level. She noticed her eyes no longer felt dry when looking at screens, and her sleep quality had also improved—the habit-building had been very effective.
subevent.location: Hong Kong, Kowloon City District - home study

subevent.name: Followed the eye-care routine and completed the fifth weekend assessment
subevent.description: At home, Yu Xiaowei carried out every part of her daily eye-care routine: the eye-care desk lamp, the 45+5 rest, and morning and evening eye yoga. The fifth weekend assessment showed that her eye fatigue was almost zero, and she could now perform the routine naturally without needing reminders. At the same time, she kept a record of the overall habit and planned to write a summary to share with her running group as part of a healthy lifestyle.
subevent.location: Hong Kong, Kowloon City District - home study

subevent.name: Execution and summary of the final day of the eye-care habit
subevent.description: As the last day of the eye-care habit implementation cycle, Yu Xiaowei carried out all the eye-care routines at home: she kept the eye-care desk lamp on throughout the day's work, made sure to look into the distance for 5 minutes after at least 4 sessions of 45 minutes of work, and completed 5 minutes of eye yoga in the morning and evening. She then made a final summary based on six months of evaluation records, concluded that she had formed a stable eye-care routine, and shared the experience with her family (Chen Meiling, Zhang Weiming), encouraging them to try it too.
subevent.location: Hong Kong, Kowloon City District - home study

subevent.name: Self-assessment of eye symptom relief
subevent.description: At the end of the year, Yu Xiaowei self-assessed the effects of her eye-care routine and noticed that the frequent dry, gritty eye symptoms she had previously experienced had significantly eased. After prolonged screen use, she no longer felt obvious discomfort, and she was satisfied with the improvement brought by sticking with the habit.
subevent.location: Hong Kong, Kowloon City District - home study

subevent.name: Recommending eye care methods to colleagues
subevent.description: During her lunch break at the AIA Insurance office, Yu Xiaowei proactively shared her six months of eye-care experience with colleague Su Lishan and several other colleagues, including specific methods such as getting glasses, using an eye-care desk lamp, and eye yoga, and encouraged her colleagues to pay attention to eye health.
subevent.location: Wan Chai District, Hong Kong - AIA office pantry

name: Assist her father in handling high-risk investment losses and asset restructuring.
description: On November 28, after learning that her father had suffered losses from purchasing high-risk products after trusting someone, Yu Xiaowei contacted the company's legal adviser to consult on the possibility of rights protection, and compiled materials such as investment contracts and fund flow statements. That evening, after discussing with her husband, she decided to set aside HK$50,000 from the family emergency fund to help her father. On November 30, she talked with her father face to face, proposed advancing HK$50,000 in installments to repay part of the principal, and suggested converting the remaining funds into low-risk wealth management products. Her father accepted the asset restructuring plan.

subevent.name: Consulting legal counsel and organizing materials
subevent.description: After learning that her father Yu Guoqiang had suffered losses from risky products he had been persuaded by others to buy, Yu Xiaowei immediately contacted Lawyer Chen, the legal consultant at her company AIA, and called to ask about the possibility of claiming compensation for the investment losses and the legal basis. Afterwards, in her home study, she sorted through the investment contracts, bank fund transfer records, and other key materials provided by her father, categorizing and filing them for later analysis.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Wan Chai District, AIA Building, and home in Kowloon City District

subevent.name: Discussing family financial strategies with her husband
subevent.description: That evening, Yu Xiaowei and her husband Zhang Weiming had a detailed discussion at home about her father's investment losses and possible legal options to protect his rights. After deliberation, the couple decided to set aside 50,000 Hong Kong dollars from the family emergency reserve to help her father repay part of the principal in installments, and planned to convert the remaining funds into low-risk wealth management products to ease her father's psychological pressure.
subevent.location: Living room at home, Kowloon City District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

subevent.name: Meeting with father to present the restructuring plan
subevent.description: According to plan, Yu Xiaowei had a one-on-one meeting with her father Yu Guoqiang in his room (at home) on the afternoon of November 30. She first calmed his anxiety, then proposed a specific asset restructuring plan: she would advance HK$50,000 in installments to help cover part of the principal loss, while suggesting that her father redeem the remaining funds from high-risk products and switch to purchasing stable wealth-management insurance products from AIA Insurance to protect principal and gain stable returns. After consideration, her father accepted the plan.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Kowloon City District - home

name: Lin Jiaxin was suddenly laid off. Yu Xiaowei accompanied her through the setback, learned about friendship boundaries, and took her to a Cantonese embroidery class to release her emotions.
description: On June 2, Lin Jiaxin suddenly received a layoff notice from her school and broke down emotionally. Yu Xiaowei went to the downstairs of her apartment that night, only to find that Lin refused to meet her. Over the following week, despite Yu Xiaowei's many texts and phone calls, she received no positive response and felt deeply the powerlessness and boundaries in friendship. It was not until June 16 that Lin Jiaxin voluntarily invited her to coffee and admitted, 'In those days I felt like the whole world was pitying me, which made me even sadder.' Yu Xiaowei learned anew how to accompany her quietly without pity. On the morning of June 21, to help Lin Jiaxin get out of her low point, Yu Xiaowei took her to a Cantonese embroidery experience class. In the quiet threading of needles, Lin Jiaxin released her pent-up emotions for the first time and completed her first small work, 'A Leaf,' but after the class she did not say she would continue participating. The relationship between the two quietly turned through the ups and downs.

subevent.name: Yu Xiaowei learned that Lin Jiaxin had been laid off and rushed to the downstairs of her home
subevent.description: During the day on June 2, Lin Jiaxin suddenly received a layoff notice from the school and broke down emotionally. That evening, after learning the news from her husband Zhang Weiming, Yu Xiaowei immediately drove from her home in Kowloon City District to the downstairs of Lin Jiaxin's residence at No. 58 Fuk Wing Street, Sham Shui Po District. However, Lin Jiaxin refused to meet, and after staying downstairs for about half an hour, Yu Xiaowei left with no choice.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - downstairs at 58 Fuk Wing Street, Sham Shui Po District

subevent.name: Yu Xiaowei made multiple attempts to contact Lin Jiaxin but received no positive response.
subevent.description: For more than a week starting June 3, Yu Xiaowei tried to contact Lin Jiaxin every day via WeChat and phone calls, but Lin Jiaxin either didn't answer or briefly replied "I'm fine" or "Let me be alone." Yu Xiaowei felt deeply helpless and confused, began reflecting on the question of boundaries in friendship, but never stopped caring. During this period, she also often confided in her mother Chen Meiling about this at home.
subevent.location: Home in Kowloon City District, Hong Kong

subevent.name: Lin Jiaxin took the initiative to invite Yu Xiaowei for coffee and opened up.
subevent.description: On the afternoon of June 16, Lin Jiaxin took the initiative to message Yu Xiaowei and ask to meet at a café in Kowloon Tong. After meeting, Lin Jiaxin admitted: 'Those days I felt like the whole world was sympathizing with me, which made me even sadder.' Yu Xiaowei said little and just listened quietly. The two re-established a friendship based on companionship rather than pity, and their relationship gradually warmed up.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Kowloon Tong District café

subevent.name: Yu Xiaowei contacted the Yue embroidery teacher in advance to book a trial class.
subevent.description: To help Lin Jiaxin release her emotions, Yu Xiaowei decided to take her to experience Cantonese embroidery, which Yu herself loved. On the evening of June 20, Yu Xiaowei contacted Ms. Wu Xiuying via WeChat, booked a two-hour trial class for the next morning, and told her about Lin Jiaxin's situation and needs. Ms. Wu welcomed the plan.
subevent.location: Home in Kowloon City District, Hong Kong

subevent.name: Yu Xiaowei took Lin Jiaxin to a Cantonese embroidery experience class, and they completed their pieces.
subevent.description: On the morning of June 21, Yu Xiaowei accompanied Lin Jiaxin to Wu Xiuying's studio on Lai Chi Kok Road in Sham Shui Po District for a Cantonese embroidery trial class. In the quiet shuttle of needles and thread, Lin Jiaxin released her suppressed emotions for the first time. With the guidance of Teacher Wu and Yu Xiaowei, she completed a small piece, A Leaf. After class, Lin Jiaxin was visibly in a better mood, but said she would not continue embroidering on a regular basis for now. The two chatted briefly outside the studio and then went home separately.
subevent.location: Hong Kong - Wu Xiuying's Studio, Lai Chi Kok Road, Sham Shui Po District

name: Team sales review and supervisory meeting
description: On Tuesday, November 11, Yu Xiaowei led the team's monthly sales review meeting. To address the new hire He Junwen's lack of execution, she announced the use of task lists and a one-on-one follow-up system, and shared the insurance case of Mr. Chen, a running buddy, emphasizing winning clients through trust and professionalism. Team morale improved somewhat, and she herself resolved to push the Shenzhen client recovery plan in the second half of the month.

subevent.name: Chaired the monthly sales review meeting.
subevent.description: Yu Xiaowei hosted the team's monthly sales review meeting in the company conference room, attended by all team members (including newcomer He Junwen and senior colleague Su Lishan). The meeting covered a review of October sales performance, analysis of successful and unsuccessful cases, and reports on the progress of new-hire training. Yu Xiaowei highlighted the case of her running buddy Mr. Chen, who purchased insurance because he trusted her professionalism, emphasizing that integrity and expertise win clients. Team morale was boosted.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Wan Chai District - AIA Building meeting room

subevent.name: Announced the new-hire follow-up system.
subevent.description: During the discussion segment of the meeting, Yu Xiaowei addressed new hire He Junwen's insufficient execution by announcing on the spot the adoption of a task list management tool and requiring weekly one-on-one follow-up coaching to improve the new hire's work execution and learning effectiveness. This system took effect immediately.
subevent.location: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region - Wan Chai District - AIA Building meeting room

subevent.name: After the meeting, formulated a customer win-back plan for Shenzhen.
subevent.description: After the meeting, Yu Xiaowei returned to her desk and, using the time before leaving work, sorted through a list of potential clients in Shenzhen and drafted a framework for a trust-based win-back plan, planning to reactivate clients in that region in the second half of the month through phone calls and in-person visits.
subevent.location: Office at AIA Building, Wan Chai District, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

name: Consulting Teacher Wu Xiuying about complex Cantonese embroidery stitches

She showed her unfinished embroidery piece 'Winter' and asked for advice on how to depict the layered texture of a snowy scene. Teacher Wu demonstrated the snowflake paving stitch and the embroidery method of gradient transition between solid and open stitching. Yu Xiaowei took careful notes and practiced on the spot, repeatedly trying different stitch densities and thread colors until late at night. This learning experience helped her break through her creative bottleneck and filled her with confidence about completing her work for the craft exhibition.

During the meal, Yu Xiaowei shared her half-marathon experience and workplace frustrations, while her husband talked about an amusing incident while repairing an air conditioner. They also discussed Christmas family travel plans, adding new warmth to their relationship.

subevent.description: From 18:30 to 20:30, Yu Xiaowei and her husband had dinner at 'Ice Room Time,' a nostalgic Hong Kong-style western restaurant in Mong Kok. Nostalgic golden oldies played in the restaurant, and they ordered the signature black pepper beef fillet, baked pork chop rice, and red wine. During the meal, Yu Xiaowei shared her recent half-marathon training experience and the frustrations of dealing with high-end clients at work, while Zhang Weiming talked about funny incidents he encountered while repairing air conditioners and clients' family trivia. name: Son Zhang Haoran’s 9th birthday party
description: To celebrate Zhang Haoran's 9th birthday, the whole family discussed plans in the living room on August 9 and decided to hold a party at the McDonald's near home on the afternoon of August 16, inviting classmates and running friend Shen Peiwen. On August 10, they notified the invitees. On August 11, they bought running shoes and a Guangdong embroidery materials kit. On August 14, they booked the venue and purchased party supplies. On the morning of August 16, they decorated the venue; in the afternoon, the party was held. After receiving gifts, the son happily changed into his new shoes and ran around. Everyone sang and cut the cake, and the atmosphere was joyful. In the evening, they cleaned up the venue and sent thank-you messages.
